articles.title: Florida Basketball Is No. 1 Again, but Can the Gators Live Up to the Hype?
articles.summary: The preseason AP Top 25 ranked Florida basketball number 1. The Gators received 47 of the 59 first-place votes, with Duke and Illinois receiving the rest. No...
articles.body:
The preseason AP Top 25 ranked Florida basketball number 1. The Gators received 47 of the 59 first-place votes, with Duke and Illinois receiving the rest. Notably, Florida last earned the preseason NO. 1 ranking before the 2006-07 season. What makes the Gators the team to beat this year?

Florida Basketball Has A Lot of Returning Talent

The Gators have four starters returning: Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon, Reuben Chinyelu, and Boogie Fland. These four players were 61.7% of the team's scoring last season. Denzel Aberdeen, who won a championship with Florida in 2025, is also returning after one year at Kentucky.

Continuity and team chemistry matter a lot in college basketball. In the last few years, we've seen the more experienced teams that have been together for a while win. The returning starters will make Todd Golden's job a lot easier. The Gators will have an easier time starting the season and clicking with each other.

Florida Wants to Forget Last Year's Tournament Exit

Florida won the SEC regular-season championship last year but followed that up with disappointment in the tournament. This happened a year after winning the National Championship. They looked poised to have another dominant year last season but fell short. They lost in the second round to the Iowa Hawkeyes.

Throughout the season, they would demonstrate championship potential. Some even had them in the championship game. Florida needs improved three-point shooting. Last season they shot 32.1% from three, one of the lowest marks in program history. Aberdeen being back should help lower their turnover number and provide consistent guard play.

Duke and Illinois Are Right Behind Florida

Duke received 10 first-place votes, and Illinois received two votes. Those are two teams that could challenge Florida this season. The Blue Devils reloaded their roster with transfers and freshmen. Illinois is building off of their roster from last season and looks even better.

The polls show Florida as the clear number one team with 47 first-place votes. The margin may be even smaller than that, as all three teams have looked really good in their preseason games. The Gators have an advantage with all of their returning players, experience, and team chemistry. They will need to show that they can outperform the elite programs.

Florida has the experience, talent, and motivation to be able to win the championship. Tough opponents and a challenging conference will test Florida this year. Those games against elite opponents will answer important questions. As of right now, their number-one ranking is justified based on their roster and all the players returning. Now they just have to go out and prove that they're the number one team.

articles.body:

articles.title: Questions linger over handling of Jalen Hurts' blood clot situation: 'He should have never played'
articles.summary: The announcement has left fans concerned primarily about Hurts' health and recovery, while also raising questions about whether he should have been cleared t...
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the season after a blood clot in his leg led to blood clots in his lungs, according to a joint statement released by the Philadelphia Eagles and his agent.

The announcement has left fans concerned primarily about Hurts' health and recovery, while also raising questions about whether he should have been cleared to play in London and travel home afterward.

"Oh, it was so heartbreaking. I feel so bad for him. I pray he's OK; that's the most important thing," said Kelly Schoch of Ocean City, New Jersey.

Hurts is now on blood thinners and will remain on them for the next few months.

"He should have never played; we'll see what happens," said Jerry Chambers of Levittown.

His team has said his prognosis is "very good."

To better understand the diagnosis, Dr. William Gray, System Chief of Cardiovascular Services at Main Line Health, discussed the condition and its treatment.

"Blood clots to the lungs can be life-threatening. Like I said, we're very fortunate the team did a great job picking this up early and on the appropriate blood thinners and on a course to full recovery," Gray said.

Hurts was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his calf the day before the game in London. Once there, he spent hours in the hospital and played the game on little sleep.

Gray said the initial diagnosis would not necessarily have prevented Hurts from playing.

"Ninety percent of people who have superficial venous thrombosis respond to conservative measures, which means compression, heat and so on," he added.

After Hurts returned home, doctors conducted further examinations and determined the clot had moved. He was subsequently ruled out of Sunday's game. The team's handling of the situation has since come under scrutiny.

"The best thing that happened was that the team taking care of him followed up when he got back to the United States and did the ultrasound, which identified the extending problem," Gray said.

Fans expressed disappointment about losing Hurts for the remainder of the season but remained hopeful about the team's prospects.

"Upset, just want to make sure he comes back healthy," said Ryan Mahler of Croydon.

According to the statement, Hurts is not expected to experience any long-term effects from the condition. He will continue to be around the team while being monitored.

articles.title: One Michigan team makes SI's all-time top 25. It's not the Wolverines
articles.summary: The ranking leaves Michigan, college football's all-time leader in victories, without a team among SI's top 25.
articles.body:
Of all the championship teams produced by Michigan's storied college football programs, only one cracked Sports Illustrated's latest ranking of the 25 greatest teams of all time.

And it didn't come from Ann Arbor, home to the winningest college program of all time.

Instead, Sports Illustrated ranked a team from Michigan State University among the greatest squads in history. SI ranked MSU's storied 1966 team 20th on its list. The team was a 9-0-1 powerhouse whose significance stretched well beyond wins and losses.

The ranking leaves Michigan, college football's all-time leader in victories, without a team among SI's top 25 despite a history filled with national champions, undefeated seasons and some of the sport's most recognizable players and coaches.

MSU 1966 team is best known for only blemish

The Spartans swept their Big Ten schedule in 1966. Their only blemish came in a 10-10 tie against Notre Dame in one of college football's most famous and most-watched games.

But SI's case for the Spartans goes beyond their performance on the field.

The ranking emphasizes the role coach Duffy Daugherty's program played in opening opportunities for Black players at a time when much of major college football remained segregated.

SI noted that the 1966 Spartans had 17 Black players, 10 of them from the South.

The team was also loaded with talent, including future College Football Hall of Famers Bubba Smith, George Webster, Clinton Jones and Gene Washington.

Michigan State outscored opponents by nearly 20 points per game, according to SI, while a defense anchored by Smith and Webster allowed 9.9 points per game. The Spartans beat No. 9 Purdue 41-20 on their way to a perfect Big Ten record.

Then came the game that would define the season.

No. 2 Michigan State and No. 1 Notre Dame played to a 10-10 tie in East Lansing in what was known as the Game of the Century. Notre Dame finished first in the final Associated Press and UPI polls, while Michigan State was recognized as national champion by the National Football Foundation and other selectors.

MSU then placed the greatest concentration of first-round NFL talent from one school in the following year's draft: Four of the NFL's first eight picks were Spartans (1. Smith, to the Colts, 2. Jones, to the Vikings, 5. Webster, to the Oilers, 8. Washington, to the Vikings).

Interestingly, SI did not select the 1966 Notre Dame team in its greatest rankings. The Fighting Irish also went 9-0-1, but SI nevertheless gave the No. 20 spot to the Spartans, whose broader impact on the integration of college football figured prominently in the magazine's assessment.

SI's assessment of the Spartans' broader legacy was unequivocal: "Michigan State forever changed the sport for the better."

For Michigan fans, the more surprising part of the ranking may be the team that isn't there.

The Wolverines have no shortage of candidates.

Fielding Yost's 1901 Michigan team went 11-0 and outscored its opponents an astounding 550-0. The following team went 11-0 and outscored opponents 644-12.

Michigan had other dominant teams in the early decades of college football, became a national power again in the 1940s and shared the 1997 national championship behind Heisman Trophy winner Charles Woodson.

And then there is the most obvious modern candidate: the 2023 Wolverines, who went 15-0 and beat Washington to win the College Football Playoff national championship.

The makeup of SI's ranking may provide some context for Michigan's absence.

Although college football dates to 1869, nine of SI's 25 selections are from 2000 or later, based on the teams included in its ranking.

Only four selections reach back before 1950. The oldest team included is Notre Dame's undefeated 1924 national champion, which ranks No. 25.

That leaves the first half-century or so of college football without a representative, a notable factor for Michigan because some of the Wolverines' most statistically overwhelming teams played during that period.

Michigan's teams from 1901 through 1904, for instance, went a combined 43-0-1. All four fall before the earliest team represented in SI's rankings.

SI acknowledged at the outset that comparing teams separated by generations presents problems. The article pointed to the dramatic evolution in offensive styles and player size as well as the gradual racial integration of college football.

There is one more wrinkle in the rankings. The 1968 Ohio State team ranks No. 10.

SI highlighted the famous "Super Sophomores" team of Rex Kern, Jim Stillwagon and Jack Tatum. Ohio State finished 10-0 and defeated USC in the Rose Bowl to complete an undefeated national championship season.

At the top of the list, SI ranks the 2001 Miami Hurricanes No. 1, followed by 1995 Nebraska, 2019 LSU, 1972 USC and 1971 Nebraska. Two of the top 25, the 2009 and 2024 Alabama teams, were coached by former MSU Coach Nick Saban.

But for football fans in Michigan, No. 20 arguably provides the ranking's most interesting takeaway. The state's representative is Daugherty's 1966 Spartans, a team remembered not only for what it accomplished on the field but for helping change who got the opportunity to play major college football.

articles.title: Dan Orlovsky blasts Commanders coach Dan Quinn for MNF 4th down mismanagement
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders faced the 5-0 49ers in San Francisco that led to a wild error in judgment by coach Dan Quinn in the second quarter. Quarterback Jay...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders faced the 5-0 49ers in San Francisco that led to a wild error in judgment by coach Dan Quinn in the second quarter. Quarterback Jayden Daniels threw the ball away on fourth down, causing an unnecessary turnover on a day when two key offensive players were hurt, including guard Sam Cosmi .

ESPN's Dan Orlovsky joined Pat McAfee at halftime to discuss what happened , and decided to call out the Commanders coach. Orlovsky yelled for Quinn to kick a field goal, but the play ended in disaster.

"We found out at halftime, Dan Quinn didn't know what down it was," McAfee said. "That's a real problem."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I'm okay with trying to see if you can draw 'em offsides…I'm a Dan Quinn guy, but you've gotta get the operation better," Orlovsky said.

The missed opportunity came back to bite Washington later in the game as they trailed 23-17 with the 49ers holding the ball and running down the clock in the fourth quarter. Commanders kicker Drew Stevens doinked in an extra point , one of the few lucky moments of the game for Quinn's team, but they seemed behind the eight-ball all night as they struggled to keep pace with San Francisco's Brock Purdy-led offense.

Star wideout Stefon Diggs also suffered a hand injury during the contest , adding to Quinn and his team's woes on a gut-check kind of evening at Levi's Stadium. Daniels picked up the slack for a lackluster running game by Quinn's team, keeping Washington in the contest with over 200 yards passing and two touchdowns as the game clock continued to tick down.

Quinn and Daniels' mental errors appeared unforgivable, but ultimately were a symptom of a high-pressure environment and a high-stakes game. Fans began to wonder if the Commanders had enough time to claw their way back into a tie, or perhaps a lead, as the fourth quarter neared its inevitable conclusion.

"Bears OG Jonah Jackson has a hip flexor injury and is considered week-to-week, per source. Status for TNF in doubt but shouldn't be long-term," Fowler wrote.

articles.title: Commanders rally falls short, lose to 49ers 23-17
articles.summary: The Commanders came from behind in the second half, but the rally comes up short at the end.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders ' rally fell short on Monday as they lost 23-17 to the San Francisco 49ers.

Jayden Daniels was sacked on the game's final play, ending the Commanders' last chance to steal a win from the undefeated 6-0 49ers.

The Commanders were completely outplayed and outcoached for the first two and a half quarters as the 49ers raced to a 23-3 lead. Then, Washington suddenly came alive on both offense and defense.

Closing out the third quarter, Washington drove 65 yards in 11 plays. The key play of the drive was a fourth-and-5 at the 49ers' 31, when Daniels found Stefon Diggs for 13 yards to the 18. Five plays later, Daniels found Diggs for a one-yard touchdown, and it was 23-10.

The Commanders' defense came alive, holding the 49ers to -1 yd in three plays, forcing a punt. Washington responded with an 80-yard drive in 10 plays. On a third-and-8 at the 49ers' 41, Daniels connected with Antonio Williams for 23 yards to the 18. A roughing-the-passer penalty moved the ball to the 9. Daniels then found Rachaad White in the middle of the field as the Commanders closed to 23-17.

This time the Commanders' defense forced a punt after the 49ers gained no yards in three plays. Daniels found Treylon Burks for 30 yards to the 49ers' 31-yard line. Jeremy McNichols then ran 31 yards for a tying touchdown with 4:19 remaining, but left guard Chris Paul was caught committing a facemask penalty, taking the score off the board.

Daniels was then sacked on fourth-and-8, but the 49ers were called for illegal contact, giving the Commanders a first down at the San Francisco 24. On fourth-and-3 at the 49ers' 17, Daniels' pass to Burke at the pylon was incomplete; contact caused Burke to drop the pass.

One final stop by the Commanders' defense forced another San Francisco punt. Daniels found White for 9 yards and Williams for 17. But the final three plays were an incompletion to stop the clock, an intentional grounding, and then Daniels was sacked by Romello Height, ending the Washington rally.

With the loss, the Commanders fall to 1-4-1 and can now get some much-needed rest during their scheduled bye week.

articles.title: Dan Quinn on viral clip: "I definitely knew it was fourth down"
articles.summary: The first half of Monday night's game included a failed fourth-and-two play by the Commanders from the San Francisco 13.
articles.body:
The first half of Monday night's game included a failed fourth-and-two play by the Commanders from the San Francisco 13. After the pass to the end zone landed incomplete and the Commanders were called for an illegal shift, ESPN's cameras caught Commanders coach Dan Quinn seemingly surprised to learn it was fourth down.

When he met with reporters nearly an hour after the game ended, Quinn was ready for the question regarding the viral lip-reading moment.

"I definitely knew it was fourth down," Quinn said. "We were going for it, and I was — I think what you're referring to, I was probably saying, like, with the illegal shift, there's not a penalty to go for a field goal. Like, it doesn't go, like, it's the turn on downs. Like, I think somebody asked me, 'Can we kick a field goal?' So, now we were going for it. We knew we had to go for some fourth downs to be bold in the game. I didn't think it was gonna be a 17-14 game. I probably thought it was gonna need 28, 30 to score, you know, to go win it. And so it was by design that we were gonna go, but I knew what happened. I think, I probably was just commenting that I remember, at least on the headset, somebody asked me, after an illegal shift, like it was turnover on downs, and [quarterback] Jayden [Daniels] saw the foul, too. He also came out and saw the penalty."

You can watch the clip and come to your own conclusion. Again, he seemed to be surprised, not stating a fact. And he clearly had his story ready when he arrived for his press conference — along with plenty of time after the game to craft it.

Obviously, after what happened last week, Quinn couldn't afford to admit he didn't know it was fourth down. Even if he didn't know it was fourth down.

articles.title: Mike Sullivan's Rangers 'building an identity' amid perfect MSG start
articles.summary: The New York Rangers improved to 6-0-0 at MSG with Monday's 5-2 win over the Anaheim Ducks and are building an identity in the process.
articles.body:
The Rangers avoided a three-game skid with Monday's 5-2 win over the Ducks, scoring 1:18 into the first period before New York's three goals in the second buried Anaheim.

"I think we had a lot of juice tonight and kind of fed off that and just kind of kept it going through 60 minutes," said RW Gabe Perreault , whose goal 10:17 into the second period padded the Rangers' 3-0 lead.

New York (7-3-1) is 6-0-0 at MSG, a stark contrast from the 2025-26 season's 14-20-7 home record that contributed to last year's 34-39-9 record and second straight postseason miss.

"When we're talking about building an identity, I think it's an identity that we can play no matter where we play," said Rangers coach Mike Sullivan . "We're trying to play a certain game out there where we dictate the terms, where we have the ability to play to our strengths. I thought we did a pretty good job tonight. We've done a pretty good job at home to this point. We have a lot of hockey in front of us and we realize that.

"... I think that we're constantly going to strive to improve and get better. But I do think our guys have a pretty clear understanding of what winning hockey looks like for our team. And I think, when you have that understanding as a group, that's when you're starting to establish an identity in the true sense of the word."

After a two-game trip in Canada with games at the Toronto Maple Leafs (Thursday) and Ottawa Senators (Saturday), New York returns to MSG and looks for 7-0-0 next Monday against the Los Angeles Kings.

"It's nice," said RW Oliver Bjorkstrand , who scored a pair of goals to boost New York's 5-0 lead in the third period. "You want to win at home. I think it's a good spot to be in for fans and just the overall momentum. So, yeah, six is really good. It's a good stretch and, naturally, we would like to keep that going."

articles.title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels Faces Backlash for Brutal Mistake Against 49ers
articles.summary: It’s been a challenging seven days or so for Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels after the way their Week 5 matchup against the New York Giants...
articles.body:
It's been a challenging seven days or so for Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels after the way their Week 5 matchup against the New York Giants ended.

Yet, early in Monday night's showdown against the San Francisco 49ers, Daniels did himself no favors in proving that his decision-making and overall football IQ are where they need to be.

In the first half, while trailing 13-3, the Commanders were in the red zone and facing fourth-and-2.

When you're going for it on fourth down, you want to make a play and extend the drive. Even taking a sack gives your receivers a chance to make something happen, because an incomplete pass or a failed conversion results in a turnover on downs anyway.

The one thing you don't want to do is fail to give your receivers a chance to make a play on the ball. That's exactly what Daniels did.

Rolling to his right, Daniels elected to throw the football sky-high and out of bounds. Although the Commanders were flagged for illegal motion on the play, completing the pass could have given them another down to attempt a field goal after San Francisco accepted the penalty, which would have made it fourth-and-7.

Instead, because Daniels threw the ball away, the 49ers declined the penalty and took possession.

ESPN announcers Joe Buck and Troy Aikman both called out Daniels for a decision that simply can't happen in that situation.

"Another game situation mistake for Jayden Daniels," Buck said on the broadcast.

"You just can't do that," Aikman added. "On 4th down you have to give one of your guys at least a chance to go get it … you can see the frustration from Dan Quinn."

Fans also took to social media to criticize Daniels for throwing the ball away on fourth down.

"Jayden Daniels actually has 0 situational awareness," one fan wrote.

Someone else added, "Did… did Jayden Daniels just throw the ball away on 4th down?! I take back anything I said about that end of game play being on coaches. Jayden's just a moron."

Another person posted, "This broadcast needs to circle back on Jayden Daniels throwing the ball away on 4th down. Doing that any week is unacceptably stupid."

articles.title: New 49ers WR 'a possibility' to return Week 7 after Mike Evans injury
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers may be getting some help on the injury front with Mike Evans dealing with an Achilles issue.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers could be getting reinforcements off Injured Reserve following Mike Evans' injury Monday night.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan on Monday after the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders indicated veteran WR Christian Kirk could be in the mix at wide receiver for the 49ers when they visit the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7.

Kirk's practice window was opened in the lead up to Week 6 and he was originally listed as questionable on the injury report. The team downgraded him to "out" before the game and didn't activate him off IR. Shanahan said Kirk has a chance to play next week.

"Yeah, he's a possibility for next week," Shanahan said. "He had two good practices in, it was just his first two practices of the year. We were down on wideouts so it's still something that we discussed, but we decided to give him another week."

Kirk was listed as limited in all three Week 6 practices. Shanahan likely called it "two" practices because the final session is only a walk-through.

Still, if Evans is going to miss time as NBC Sports Bay Area's Jennifer Lee Chan reported, it would make sense that they'd activate Kirk if he's healthy after missing all of training camp and the first five weeks of the regular season with a calf strain. Without Evans or Kirk, the 49ers have Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing healthy on the active roster at receiver. Veteran Malik Turner was up from the practice squad for Monday's game as well.

The 49ers receiving corps has been beat up all season long, and now they have even more complications in that group heading into Week 7. Activating Kirk could alleviate some of those issues.

articles.title: Collin Sexton reveals eye-opening area of focus to bring ‘energy’ to Lakers
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers haven’t yet gotten to see how Collin Sexton fits in with the rotation as the nine-year veteran has been sidelined for th...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers haven't yet gotten to see how Collin Sexton fits in with the rotation as the nine-year veteran has been sidelined for the entirety of the team's preseason schedule while recovering from a lower leg injury. But Sexton was a full participant during Lakers' practice on Monday, trending in the right direction for him to potentially make his purple and gold debut on Wednesday night when the Lakers open the season at home against the Golden State Warriors.

The Lakers' regular starting lineup has not yet been finalized, with only Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler as the certainties. But it's possible that with Collin Sexton back from injury, that Quentin Grimes will move into the Lakers' starting lineup with Sexton being able to anchor the bench as the ball-handler.

Turnovers had been an issue with the team during preseason, and head coach JJ Redick opted to go with Grimes off the bench in the preseason finale to try and cut down turnovers while providing the second unit with a capable ball-handler.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

While Sexton certainly will help in terms of ball-handling and scoring the ball, there is one particular area of focus where he feels he can make a major impact this season.

"I can see where I can fit in pretty easily. I think even just on the defensive side, bringing that energy, bringing that juice and trying to disrupt. Not always turning the ball over and getting someone to turn it over, but just disrupt and being the clock down," Sexton said following Lakers' practice on Monday. "And offensively, getting into the paint. I think that's something that I have done really well in my career. And then spacing, making sure I'm spacing for the guys, Luka, AR, even when Walker gets it in the pocket, being ready to shoot on that backside. Just finding ways to help the team."

Sexton bounced around last season, beginning the year with the Charlotte Hornets before being traded to the Chicago Bulls at the trade deadline. In total, he appeared in 68 games including 22 starts, at a little over 23 minutes per game. He averaged 15.4 points, 2.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.1 steals with splits of 48.5 percent shooting from the field, 40.1 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 85.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line.

The former Alabama standout has always been a reliable scoring threat throughout his career, and a rather efficient one too with career averages of 47.2 percent shooting from the field and 38.9 percent shooting from the 3-point line. But he hasn't always been known for his defensive acumen.

Perhaps a big reason for that was the fact that he's been asked to be one of the team's primary scoring options at his other stops. Here with the Lakers, he doesn't have to do so much offensively. He can focus on defense and hone in on being a defensive 'pest' as he called it back during media day.

"I would say coming in with the right approach. Every day is not going to be perfect, but making sure that every day is a lesson. And I think just watching a lot of film on other guys and making sure that I know certain people's tendencies," Sexton said. "That's something that me and JJ … we've been talking about. Know people's tendencies, watch a lot of film and make sure when you're out there you know what they like to do, what they don't like to do and that's gonna help you become a better defender."

articles.title: Stefon Diggs posts six catches in his return to the lineup
articles.summary: Stefon Diggs put up a 6-44-1 line in his return from injury in Week 6 as the Commanders lost to the 49ers on Monday Night Football.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders WR Stefon Diggs caught six passes (on seven targets) for 44 yards and a touchdown during the team's Week 6 loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Why It Matters: Diggs returned from a one-game absence to finish second on the club in receptions and fourth in yards while also securing his fourth touchdown catch of the season. With Terry McLaurin (knee) being carted off, Diggs suddenly finds himself in position to slide into the nominal WR1 role in Washington with Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams likely moving into expanded roles as well. The Commanders are off in Week 7, so we won't see what a post-McLaurin passing attack looks like for a couple of weeks, but Diggs is well positioned to become a decent WR3 for fantasy owners going forward.

articles.title: 49ers nearly let 6-0 slip away in 23-17 win as Commanders' comeback falls short
articles.summary: The 49ers built a big first-half lead over the Commanders, but the offense disappeared in the second half and a much-flagged defense barely fended off Washin...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers nearly blew a 20-point lead against the Washington Commanders on Monday night at Levi's Stadium, but they held on to win 23-17 and improve to 6-0 on the season.

After going up 23-3 early in the second half, the 49ers allowed two consecutive touchdowns that cut Washington's deficit to six. A large reason for those struggles? Penalties. San Francisco committed 11 infractions for 88 yards on Monday, many of which came in crucial moments.

Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels, after largely being held in check early, exploded in the second half, finishing the night with a 72.5% completion rate, 300 passing yards and two touchdowns.

The bulk of Daniels' production came on three of Washington's final four drives. He first led an 11-play, 56-yard drive for a score. Then, a 10-play, 66-yard march to the end zone.

Finally, with four minutes to go, Commanders running back Jeremy McNichols broke free and scampered to the end zone for what would have been a game-tying touchdown. But a facemask on guard Chris Paul negated the score. With the ball at the Niners' 29-yard line, rookie defensive end Romello Height collected a fourth-down sack on Daniels, which would have essentially sealed the result… but a penalty on safety Ashtyn Davis gave the Commanders yet another life.

It looked like the 49ers were going to have an epic meltdown. The Commanders were down six with the ball in the red zone. But 49ers safety Malik Mustapha, who broke out last Sunday in the 49ers' 32-29 win over the Seattle Seahawks, made two plays that got the 49ers' defense off the field. First, he delivered a crushing hit in the box on McNichols on third down, followed by a pass breakup in the end zone on receiver Treylon Burks on fourth down.

The Commanders got one last chance in the final minute and worked their way back into 49ers territory, but an intentional grounding call on Daniels moved the ball back 12 yards. On the game's final play, Height and Keion White teamed up for a game-sealing sack, the 49ers' fourth of the game.

articles.title: Jordin Canada After Near Triple-Double in Finals Win: ‘I Don’t Think I Played Well’
articles.summary: Jordin Canada had 13 points, 7 rebounds and 10 assists in Atlanta’s first Finals win, but said she still did not think she played well.
articles.body:
Jordin Canada was 3 rebounds from a triple-double Monday night, finishing with 13 points, 7 rebounds, and 10 assists as the Atlanta Dream topped the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 at Chase Center.

Canada went 3-of-14 from the field and 2-of-6 from 3-point range in a team-high 35:40. She had 4 turnovers. All 5 of her made free throws came in the fourth quarter, when she went 5-of-6 at the line.

The win tied the WNBA Finals at 1-1 and was the first Finals win in franchise history.

Canada said the Dream feed off Angel Reese's energy, and she watched Reese set the tone for the rest of the team on Monday.

"Honestly, I don't think I played well," Canada said. "I think I forced a lot of tough shots for myself. I feel like I was just over thinking a lot. Defensively, I felt like I was giving a lot of opportunities for them to get downhill. I wasn't being as aggressive as I should have been, and then timely turnovers down the stretch."

"So I feel like I could have played a lot better," Canada continued. "The stats looks like I had a triple-double but to me, I know I could have played a lot better. But I'm just glad that we came together as a team. We were able to win. But next game, I'll definitely be better offensively and defensively."

Canada Still Controlled Large Stretches of Game 2

Canada's first 3-pointer, off a Reese pass with 3:46 left in the first quarter, tied the game at 13. She played all 10 minutes of the second quarter and all 10 of the fourth.

Five of Canada's 10 assists came in the second quarter. Two of those set up Allisha Gray 3-pointers in transition, and another found DeWanna Bonner for a 19-foot pull-up that put Atlanta ahead 39-37 at the half.

By the end of the night, Canada had assisted on 4 baskets each for Reese and Gray, plus one apiece for Rhyne Howard and Bonner. Atlanta finished with 17 assists.

With 3.1 seconds left in the third quarter, Canada stole a Tiffany Hayes pass. She pulled up from 32 feet and made it with 0.8 seconds remaining, sending the Dream to the fourth up 60-46.

Two of her turnovers came 28 seconds apart late in the fourth quarter, with Atlanta ahead by 17. Hayes and Gabby Williams came away with the steals, and the Valkyries got 2 points out of the pair.

With 2:14 left, the Dream challenged a shooting foul called on Canada. The call stood, and Hayes made 1 of 2 free throws.

Canada Has Delivered in Big Playoff Moments

In Game 1, Canada had 8 points, 7 assists, and 5 rebounds and hit a 13-foot jumper with 4:23 left, according to The Associated Press . Golden State won that game 68-64 .

Earlier in these playoffs, Canada scored 13 of her 19 points in the fourth quarter as Atlanta finished a first-round sweep of the Washington Mystics.

Atlanta shot 21-of-62 from the field Monday, and Golden State went 21-of-61.

Dream coach Karl Smesko said the players took what the staff emphasized on film and made it work on the floor.

"I don't have the answer to that," Smesko said. "I do know both teams are defending at a really high level with a really high intensity. So you may rush your shot. They are closing out hard. Could be a lot of factors. Maybe just both teams are settling in."

"But we'll keep track of how we're generating good shots, and as long as we are generating good shots, we feel good about it," Smesko added. "We know we have good shooters. We know we have good attackers. And we know we can get extra possessions if we are doing the things that we need to do. So we'll go back to Atlanta and hopefully — and we'll have to; we'll have to play even better, and our team realizes that. We know how good Golden State is."

Canada was called for 3 fouls and had 1 steal in the win.

Atlanta is 6-1 in the postseason heading into Game 3 on Wednesday at State Farm Arena.

articles.title: David Sánchez, sobre el arbitraje del Madrid - Sevilla: “Fue un mangazo”
articles.standfirst: El periodista de Radio MARCA criticó la no expulsión de Arda Güler, calificó lo sucedido en el Bernabéu de “fallo arbitral grosero” y cargó contra las teorías de una conspiración contra el Real Madrid
articles.summary: El periodista de Radio MARCA criticó la no expulsión de Arda Güler, calificó lo sucedido en el Bernabéu de “fallo arbitral grosero” y cargó contra las teorías de una conspiración contra el Real Madrid
articles.body: David Sánchez no tiene dudas sobre lo ocurrido en el Real Madrid - Sevilla. El presentador de DSF considera que el conjunto de Luis García Plaza resultó gravemente perjudicado por las decisiones arbitrales del Santiago Bernabéu y señaló directamente la acción de Arda Güler como el momento que condicionó el encuentro. Una polémica que, a su juicio, también desmonta el discurso de quienes denuncian una persecución arbitral contra el equipo blanco. En sus habituales Picotazos de La Tribu, Sánchez fue tajante: “Por mucho que lo del sábado ante el Sevilla se intente enmascarar en un fallo de la realización televisiva, no, es un mangazo y es un picotazo del Real Madrid al equipo de Luis García Plaza”. El periodista situó la no expulsión del futbolista turco en el centro de sus críticas. “A raíz de la no expulsión de Güler, todo cambia y nada vale”, afirmó, convencido de que esa decisión alteró el desarrollo del encuentro. Sánchez defendió las protestas del conjunto hispalense: “El Sevilla y el sevillismo están en su perfecto derecho de poner el grito en el cielo”, aseguró. Y explicó el motivo: “Les perjudicaron gravemente en ese partido ante el Real Madrid”. Tampoco aceptó que la polémica se atribuya exclusivamente a la falta de imágenes de la retransmisión. “Por mucho que lo intenten disfrazar de fallo televisivo, no, es un fallo arbitral, grosero, que perjudica al Sevilla”, insistió. La crítica de David Sánchez fue más allá del partido. El periodista de Radio MARCA mostró su cansancio con el debate arbitral que rodea al Real Madrid desde el inicio del campeonato. “El tema del arbitraje, del VAR, de la conspiración que ven ciertas facciones del madridismo empieza a ser agotador y empieza a ser cansino”, lamentó. “Y eso que estamos tan solo en la novena jornada de Liga”, añadió. Para Sánchez, lo sucedido ante el Sevilla demuestra que los errores arbitrales no responden necesariamente a una persecución contra un equipo. “Esto no va de conspiraciones en contra del Madrid. Los árbitros se equivocan, a veces a tu favor y otras veces en contra”, explicó. El presentador de DSF también reconoció que el Barcelona se beneficia de decisiones polémicas. Sin embargo, criticó la interpretación que hacen determinados sectores madridistas cuando esas jugadas favorecen a los azulgranas. “La única diferencia es que entonces el madridismo esto lo ve como una conspiración y como la continuación de la etapa Negreira”, sostuvo. Sánchez quiso dejar clara su opinión sobre los dos grandes del fútbol español. “Al Barça y al Madrid son a los dos equipos que más les ayudan los árbitros”, aseguró. Incluso fue más lejos al valorar la historia de la competición: “A lo largo de cien años es el Madrid quien más ayudas ha recibido, se pongan como se pongan”, afirmó, dejando una de las declaraciones más contundentes de su intervención. A su juicio, el encuentro contra el Sevilla debería servir para abandonar las acusaciones de persecución arbitral. “Ha desmontado la teoría de la conspiración el partido ante el Sevilla. El próximo fin de semana palmará el Madrid y vuelta la burra al trigo. Volveremos con el tema arbitral”, pronosticó.

articles.title: REDs: how relative energy deficiency in sport affects athletes
articles.summary: British long-distance runner Jake Smith was enduring a relentless pattern of race, illness, injury, repeat - he had no idea he had REDs and was under-fuelling.
articles.body:
Warning: this article contains discussion of eating disorders

"If you keep this up, you'll be in a wheelchair at 30."

That is what doctors told British long-distance runner Jake Smith four years ago.

From the outside looking in, his career was flying.

By the age of 23, he had signed a professional contract with Nike and represented Great Britain on the global stage.

But at the same time, his body was deteriorating - enduring a relentless pattern of race, illness, injury, repeat.

Balancing an intense training regime with disordered eating meant the 28-year-old returned from a running camp in Uganda weighing just eight stone (51kg) at 5ft 5in (1.7m). He had such brittle bones that he was told his career could be over.

After suffering two stress fractures in the space of four months, Smith sought professional help and was diagnosed with REDs – relative energy deficiency in sport.

It is a syndrome that can affect anyone and if left undiagnosed or untreated, can have an impact on performance and cause serious, long-lasting health problems.

The symptoms are slightly better documented in women - just last month, tennis player Emma Navarro revealed her diagnosis and subsequent decision to step away from competition until 2027.

But men are just as susceptible and due to stigma and lack of obvious warning signs, it can go undetected for longer and means many, like Smith, suffer in silence.

BBC Sport explains what the condition is, how it affects men and women and why, despite its prevalence and severity, REDs remains a relatively under-reported and overlooked area of sports science.

REDs can cause bone stress injuries, disrupted sleep, fatigue and low mood. Left untreated, the condition can lead to serious long-term health problems, including osteoporosis, cardiovascular disease and fertility issues.

Dr Nicky Keay, an expert in hormone health, says many of these symptoms stem from hormonal disruption caused by insufficient energy intake.

"Hormones go to every single bit in your body. So, if your hormones are not working well for you, you're going to feel it in all sorts of different areas," she says.

"In order to have healthy hormones, they need to be fed regularly. If you're not doing that and there's an energy deficit, often some of those hormone systems will slow down or shut down completely."

Women have a monthly barometer of their hormone health with the menstrual cycle, described by Keay as a "free monthly medical check".

Put simply, she says, a woman suffering from REDs has her periods "switched off".

For men, it is more subtle – testosterone levels will drop, resulting in a reduced libido and fatigue.

The impact on a woman's period is why the condition was first referred to in the early 1990s as the "female athlete triad".

But it was renamed by the International Olympic Committee in 2014 to acknowledge the broader range of symptoms of energy deficiency and that it also harms male athletes.

"We realised we were ignoring the other half of the population," Keay says.

"It's a strange situation because normally it's women's health that is the one being ignored but, in this situation, it's the men who weren't being recognised or represented."

Twelve years later that decision appears to be vindicated, with recent research highlighting the prevalence in men.

Meta-analysis published in Australian journal Sports Medicine last year, following a study involving thousands of elite and amateur athletes around the world, indicated 44.2% of female athletes and 49.4% of male athletes had low energy availability.

One of the answers lies in the phrase 'lighter is faster'.

For decades, it had been an accepted wisdom in sports like endurance running, cycling, climbing, horse riding, dancing and aesthetic sports like diving and gymnastics.

And for athletes like Smith, it is how his problems started.

"I believed it for years. I thought that was the way forward," he says.

"I started thinking 'how do I improve my half marathon by 10 seconds? Is it a drop in weight?'. And that's when my head completely went."

When it comes to choosing energy to cover training demand or energy to stay healthy, the body has learned through evolution and threat of predators to always prioritise movement.

It means that athletes can drop weight and still train and exercise and achieve good results.

Described by Keay as "fool's gold", the body will adjust to the energy deficit and cause a drop in performance and high risk of injuries.

Olympic and world champion Jonny Brownlee acknowledges under-fuelling mistakes he made in his triathlon career contributed to serious injuries.

"I didn't see the importance of it. Training came first and I think we weren't educated enough in how important fuelling was," he tells BBC Sport.

"You were seen, culturally, as a bit weak if you were fuelling on the bike. And the impact of that was definitely injuries - probably not recovering from my training quite as well as I should have done, stress responses, stress fractures. So there's that side of it and probably underperformance in races as well."

Brownlee, who recently announced his retirement, believes the culture of not fuelling on the bike has now changed but a stigma lingers around REDs and the perception that it is a "female issue".

"In females, there are more obvious signs but in males it can go under the radar a little bit and then it hits you by a really serious injury," he says.

"I think there's a stigma attached in there, or it's not looked at as the obvious answer to some of your problems, it's found later down the line. Men also don't like to talk about under-fuelling because it's just seen as 'you probably should feel better and you should be on top of that'."

It is those attitudes among male athletes that prompted Keay to conduct an experiment in 2019.

Assessing 50 male competitive cyclists, Keay found in her initial screenings that nearly half had poor bone health and 25% were suffering from REDs.

The cyclists were then split into two groups and across a six-month period, one half continued their training and fuelling habits as before while the others were tutored by Keay and offered nutrition and training advice.

"The group that I left to their own devices unfortunately went on the default and they lost even more bone mineral density, similar to an astronaut in space… And they performed OK, but relative to their functional threshold power, they didn't get the race results that you would have expected.

"For the group I took under my wing, there was an improvement in their bone health and really good race results.

"So, I had evidence that REDs definitely does exist quite extensively in my group of the male cyclists and you're going to underperform if you don't fuel sufficiently. The good news is that REDs is reversible. But if you don't take action, it's a decline."

As the syndrome and its symptoms are still not commonly known, it is often difficult to know where to find help.

After former GB runner Pippa Woolven's struggles with the condition, she set up a website called Project REDs which offers information and practical resources for athletes, coaches, parents and healthcare professionals.

Keay also helps people competing at all levels to recover from REDs. Most of her patients are women, but she is starting to see more men reach out for help who, she says, are often in "bad shape".

"I think the men are maybe more reluctant than the women, or maybe they don't realise they've got it. Sometimes they might use a different word for it, they say burnout," Keay says.

"I don't mind that though because there is definitely a psychological aspect to REDs. Why are you doing this? Why are you not eating the carbohydrates?"

Sometimes, it's hard to answer those questions because the under-fuelling is unintentional, either from not understanding or underestimating energy requirements or failing to match an increase in the intensity or duration of exercise with higher calorie or carbohydrate intake.

For others, former British cycling champion Brian Smith among them, the answer comes from intention.

Competing in the road race for Great Britain at the 1996 Olympics should have been the highlight of his career but, behind the scenes of the success, Smith was suffering with an eating disorder and serious mental health condition called bulimia – something he believes he developed from his sport's obsession with weight.

"I always felt like I was overweight. Everybody was under pressure regarding weight, but nobody really spoke about it," he says.

"I'm just under six foot and I've got large glutes and thigh muscles. As a road cyclist, I used to race at 68kg and for my height and build, that's quite skinny. I even got down to about 66kg and when I got down to that, I felt underpowered, I felt bad."

Smith, now 59, only discovered he had been suffering from REDs during his career when he started running eight years ago and developed three severe stress fractures, including one in his femur.

Such has been the toll on his body that Smith says he would now never encourage anyone to pursue a career as a professional cyclist.

"It really is not healthy," he says. "If you want to go to the highest levels of the sport, you will suffer later on in life. You're destroying your body.

"Sporting teams don't care - all they're worried about is performance. So they will nurture a rider, they will feed a rider, they'll get a rider to be a certain weight. They don't care about what happens to them later in life.

"I'm suffering now and I've so many regrets. I just wish I'd known more about this."

While Smith believes his sport has a long way to go in changing attitudes, British Cycling says a lot of progress has been made through education that starts at academy level and annual physical and psychological screenings.

"One of the big things we've done in the past 10 years is try and turn this into a performance-related conversation," Dr Nigel Jones, British Cycling chief medical officer, tells BBC Sport.

"Now, we couch the conversation with an athlete around 'if you under-fuel, you will not be able to perform at your best', whereas previously, conversations in power-to-weight ratio sports might have been 'you need to be lighter'.

"I think it would be naive to say REDs is never going to be an issue. But I would like to believe that its prevalence will reduce with the work that we're doing," he adds.

British Cycling is not alone in this approach, with World Climbing taking things a step further two years ago with the introduction of mandatory health checks on athletes.

Using a combination of pre-season questionnaires and 'random and targeted' screenings at competitions - similar to the way doping tests are enforced – climbers at World Championship or World Cup-level competitions are monitored for any indicators of low energy availability or REDs and could be prevented from competing if they are not deemed to be healthy.

The policy was drawn up by expert Professor Naama Constantini, who says she is "proud" of the move by World Climbing and believes other federations should follow suit.

"We are trying to educate and prevent. I'm not a policeman and we're not looking for cheaters. I'm a medical doctor and we want to make sure our athletes are healthy," she says.

"Prevention is the best medicine you can give. We want athletes and coaches to understand that it's not about weight. It's about strength, it's about performance and fuelling the body and you pay a price if you lose weight in an unhealthy way."

With more awareness and education, it is hoped the tide can be turned on REDs.

But many still suffer in ignorance, as well as silence. That is what motivates Jake Smith to keep sharing his recovery on social media, with hundreds of men and women messaging him for advice and support.

Smith has managed to reverse his condition and is now racing better than ever, recently completing the Berlin marathon in a personal-best time of two hours, nine minutes and 24 seconds.

The big goal is the 2028 Olympics, but he is adamant that the priority is making sure he stands on every start line as healthy as possible.

"I'd never want to see an athlete go through the years I've had. I'm 10-15 kilos heavier than I've ever been and the biggest thing I can say is I've never been so happy. You need a healthy body to do everything else.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story you can visit BBC Action Line.

articles.title: Sylvinho se rinde a Lamine Yamal: "No es normal lo que está haciendo"
articles.standfirst: El exfutbolista del Barcelona elogió en 'La Tribu' el talento y la evolución del extremo azulgrana, analizó el duelo ante el PSG y advirtió de que el Real Madrid puede hacer daño en el Clásico
articles.summary: El exfutbolista del Barcelona elogió en 'La Tribu' el talento y la evolución del extremo azulgrana, analizó el duelo ante el PSG y advirtió de que el Real Madrid puede hacer daño en el Clásico
articles.body: Sylvinho conoce perfectamente lo que significa jugar en el Barcelona y sabe reconocer a un futbolista especial. El brasileño atendió a La Tribu de Radio MARCA en la previa del PSG - Barça y mostró su admiración por Lamine Yamal, una de las grandes estrellas del equipo de Hansi Flick. El exseleccionador de Albania no escondió su asombro ante el talento del joven internacional español. “No, no es normal. Este tipo de jugadores son diferentes, muy diferentes”, aseguró cuando le preguntaron por Lamine. Y, lejos de considerar que el extremo haya alcanzado su techo, lanzó una advertencia sobre su progresión: “Cada día mejor”. Sylvinho destacó que el crecimiento del futbolista no se limita a sus cualidades técnicas. También está adquiriendo una madurez que le permite interpretar mejor los partidos y aprovechar sus virtudes: “Escucho entrevistas de entrenadores como Hansi Flick y Luis de la Fuente, y se escucha que el jugador va creciendo”, explicó. El brasileño incidió especialmente en la experiencia que está acumulando pese a su juventud: “Va adquiriendo experiencia, sabe dónde tiene que entrar o no. Va creciendo y creciendo”. Incluso considera que su evolución puede llevarle a ocupar otras posiciones sobre el terreno de juego. “Dentro de poco también ya le van a buscar otro lugar para jugar”, apuntó. Sylvinho terminó su reflexión con otro elogio: “Estos jugadores son magníficos, les cambia la carrera rápidamente”. Y remató: “Es un pedazo de jugador”. El brasileño tampoco quiso elegir un favorito para el enfrentamiento europeo. Preguntado por cuál de los dos equipos considera superior, respondió sin dudar: “Los dos. Son un equipazo, podría ser la final de Champions”. Sylvinho situó al Barcelona y al PSG entre los grandes referentes ofensivos del continente, junto al Bayern de Múnich. Su principal virtud, explicó, es que no se limitan a generar ocasiones, sino que tienen una capacidad extraordinaria para convertirlas. “El Barça y el PSG son equipos que producen mucho fútbol, generan mucho fútbol”, afirmó. Y advirtió del peligro de enfrentarse a conjuntos con tanta pegada: “Un día te caen cuatro o cinco”. Sobre el extraordinario inicio de temporada azulgrana, Sylvinho encontró una explicación sencilla: “Porque gana, porque gana muchos partidos. Meten cuatro o cinco goles, ¿cómo va a perder? Hay que meter el sexto”. También elogió el trabajo de Flick: “Un grandísimo entrenador, muy valiente y sabe jugar muy bien con el ADN de Barcelona. Es un equipo letal, un equipo que juega a 50 metros, muy adelantado”, destacó. Para Sylvinho, la continuidad de esa propuesta ofensiva y el trabajo acumulado permiten que los jugadores ejecuten los movimientos con naturalidad. Con el Real Madrid en el horizonte, Sylvinho evitó trasladar la superioridad futbolística del Barcelona a un pronóstico para el Clásico: “Es un partido que cualquiera te puede hacer daño de una parte o de la otra". El brasileño recordó que estos encuentros tienen características especiales: “Puede pasar todo. Hay mucha rivalidad”. Para el exazulgrana, la calidad individual puede decidir cualquier acción: “Con dos segundos de más encajas un gol o haces un gol”. Por eso espera un enfrentamiento abierto, con “mucha calidad técnica en el campo”. También tuvo palabras para Vinicius, al que conoce de su etapa en el fútbol brasileño. Sylvinho confía en que el madridista pueda recuperar su mejor versión después de atravesar un periodo complicado. “Vinicius también es bastante joven”, recordó, antes de relativizar sus dificultades actuales: “Suele pasar, un bajón o hay algo y de repente vuelven, porque hay mucha calidad. Es muy normal un bajón en un momento de la vida de un futbolista de este nivel”, concluyó.

articles.title: Rugby League World Cup: Mikey Lewis absent again as England unchanged for clash vs France despite opening defeat
articles.summary: England take on France in Perth on Saturday (7.35am kick-off BST) for second Rugby League World Cup fixture, having been thrashed by Tonga in opener; England play Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on October 30; England Women began their campaign with big win vs Wales in Perth
articles.body:
AJ Brimson retains the job at full-back with Jack Welsby again named as an interchange, while Luke Thompson starts at prop in the absence of Morgan Knowles, who suffered an injury in the lead-up to the opening game against Tonga.

Veteran centre Kallum Watkins is listed among the reserves as he chases a cap at his fourth World Cup, while there also remains no place in the squad for Mikey Lewis.

As per World Cup rules, each side is able to name a six-player bench in each game, but only four of the six players named can be brought on.

Last weekend against Tonga, Welsby and Warrington Wolves winger Matty Ashton were the unused substitutes - with Wigan Warriors speedster Zach Eckersley getting the nod instead.

For France, Toulouse playmaker Thomas Lacans has been promoted to start at five-eighth with Cesar Rouge moving to the bench.

Romeo Tropis comes in at centre, so Guillermo Aispuro-Bichet pushes out to the wing and Leo Darrelatour makes way.

Skipper Ben Garcia moves from hooker to lock and Amir Bourouh joins the starting side at No 9. A change in the front-row sees Julian Bousquet come in at prop for Lambert Belmas, who goes to the bench.

England: AJ Brimson, Dom Young, Hugo Savala, Herbie Farnworth, Zach Eckersley, George Williams, Harry Smith, Max King, Brad O'Neill, Luke Thompson, Junior Nsemba, Kai Pearce-Paul, Victor Radley.

Interchange: Jez Litten, Ben Currie, Ethan Havard, Sam Walters, Jack Welsby, Matty Ashton.

France: Arthur Mourgue, Guillermo Aispuro-Bichet, Latrell Siegwalt, Roméo Tropis, Benjamin Laguerre, Thomas Lacans, Théo Fages, Romain Navarrete, Amir Bourouh, Julian Bousquet, Arthur Romano, Mathieu Jussaume, Benjamin Garcia (c).

Interchange: César Rougé, Lambert Belmas, Mathieu Cozza, Louis Grossemy.

Teenager Foubister to start as England Women face Australia

For the England Women side, head coach Stuart Barrow has made a shock selection call at half-back, calling in 19-year-old Jenna Foubister to wear the No 7 and partner Isabel Rowe in the halves against Australia on Saturday.

Foubister was named Woman of Steel after a standout year in the Super League and came off the bench in last week's win over Wales. Georgia Roche shifts to the interchange as a result.

Molly Jones has been named to replace Georgia Wilson in the centres while Liv Wood steps in at prop in place of Mary Coleman. Lucie Sams is the new face on the interchange.

For Australia, Dragons recruit Makenzie Weale and former sevens star Sariah Paki are in line for Test debuts after being named on the interchange for the clash with England.

Coach Jess Skinner has made a handful of changes to the side that defeated Samoa last week, with Abbi Church coming in on the wing and Julia Robinson shifting to centre. Jess Sergis has been rested. Tiana Penitani Gray will line up in the back-row with Kezie Apps rested, while Quincy Dodd has also come on to the bench.

articles.title: Glenn Irwin: Northern Ireland rider backs himself to bounce back after 'hard' year
articles.summary: Glenn Irwin believes he can return to the front of the British Superbike Championship, with an exciting move to Michael Laverty's BMW-backed team providing fresh motivation for 2027.
articles.body:
Glenn Irwin believes he can return to the front of the British Superbike Championship, with an exciting move to Michael Laverty's BMW-backed team providing fresh motivation for 2027.

The 12-time North West 200 Superbike race winner will ride an Alpha Racing-prepared BMW M 1000 RR for the GRYD Racing team, co-owned by Laverty and David Eltherington.

The 36-year-old Northern Ireland rider admits 2026 failed to live up to expectations as injuries, crashes, technical issues and a difficult relationship with Ducati's new Panigale V4R, combined to derail his title ambitions.

Despite showing flashes of his speed with a podium at Knockhill and success at the North West 200, Irwin was left searching for answers throughout a frustrating campaign and ended 14th in the series standings.

The Carrickfergus rider has twice finished runner-up in BSB, including being pipped by half-a-point by then teammate Tommy Bridewell in 2023.

"It's been hard," he reflected of his 2026 season on the BBC Bikes podcast.

"There were moments when doubts came in, because that's natural as a sports person, but there were also moments this year when you realise you shouldn't have those doubts."

Those doubts also extended to his future.

After a disappointing season by his own high standards, Irwin admitted he was concerned about whether the right opportunity would emerge for 2027.

However, the chance to join Michael Laverty's team alongside Englishman Storm Stacey quickly convinced him it was the fresh start he needed.

"Storm's a great team-mate," added Irwin.

"I'm looking forward to taking from him and also passing on to him."

Listen to Glenn Irwin on the BBC Bikes podcast

'We've done it before and we can do it again'

Another significant factor in Irwin's decision was the North West 200.

The event remains hugely important to the county Antrim rider and he wanted a package capable of competing at the front in both British Superbikes and road racing.

BMW's proven strength around the NW200 circuit, coupled with Stacey's impressive performances there, made the move even more appealing.

While excitement surrounds the new challenge, Irwin is under no illusions about what lies ahead, although he does believe the combination of experience, renewed confidence and a fresh start can help him fight his way back to winning ways.

"Of course, you have to perform," he said.

"The whippersnappers are coming up through and you can either step aside and let them take your job or you can fight.

"You look at people like Leon Haslam and Tommy Bridewell. You can continue to get better in this sport. If you want to stay in it, you have to.

"The expectation is there because we know what we can do. We've done it before and we can do it again."

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal clinched a bronze medal in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday, securing India's second medal in swimming at the continental showpiece.The 22-year-old from Rohtak clocked 5 minutes and 10.91 seconds to finish third in the four-swimmer field. A political science graduate from Delhi University's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he initially pursued judo and won medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.He competes in the S11 classification, which is for swimmers with near-total visual impairment. articles.summary: Oro de Xavier Torres en categoría Sub'19 y bronce del doble scull mixto Sub'19 de Alfredo Mena y Blanca López
articles.body: Esther Briz y Ander Martín, actuales campeones de Europa, no pudieron subir al podio en los Mundiales de remo de mar (beach sprint) de Qingdao (China) al perder en cuartos de final de las pruebas individuales, en tanto que Xavier Torres se proclamó campeón individual en categoría sub-19. La remera aragonesa cumplió los pronósticos en octavos de final ante la canadiense Carling Zeeman, pero no pudo en una eliminatoria muy ajustada de cuartos ante la china Zhu Wenjie, que a la postre fue subcampeona al ceder en la final ante la australiana Isabella Scammell, primera campeona de su país en esta disciplina que se estrenará en los Juegos Olímpicos en Los Ángeles 2028. El bronce fue para la austríaca Magdalena Lobnig. En categoría absoluta masculina, Ander Martín, que llegaba también con la vitola de subcampeón universal pero que tuvo que afrontar un mar con mucho más oleaje que cuando ganó el oro continental, ganó en octavos al francés Antoine Lefebvre por diez segundos y perdió por nueve con el chino Liu Jiayu, quien posteriormente se hizo con el oro al derrotar en la final al australiano Samuel Forbes. El alemán Mortiz Wolff cerró el podio. Una de las grandes alegrías para la selección española la dio Xavi Torres. El palista del Club Náutico de Santa Pola (Alicante) se tomó la revancha de los Europeos al proclamarse campeón después de derrotar este martes a Cai Chun, de Hong Kong y al chino Bu Boren por segundos en ambos casos, y en la final venció al griego Iason Mouselimis por tres. "Es el mejor momento de mi vida. Puedo oír a mi familia, que ha venido desde España; tener a mi equipo a mi lado y a toda la gente que me apoya... Simplemente estoy muy agradecido", dijo un cansado pero feliz palista español. En doble sculls mixto categoría absoluta Teresa Díaz y Miguel Salas repitieron el cuarto puesto de los Europeos de La Línea de la Concepción. Tras ganar en octavos a los británicos Heather Gordon y James Cox y en octavos a los neerlandeses Isabel van Opzeeland y Michiel Mantel, perdieron en semifinales ante los potentes lituanos Martyna Kazlauskaite y Dominykas Jancionis y en la lucha por el bronce no pudieron con los polacos Dominika Baranowska y Adam Bujnowski. En el cuatro mixto, Adrián Miramón, Ignacio Ramón-Borja, María Ángeles Macián, Alejandra García y Ainhoa Casanova perdieron en cuartos ante el equipo chino por menos de un segundo en un enfrentamiento vibrante. Los asiáticos acabaron por lograr la plata al no poder con los imparables estadounidenses, que revalidaron su corona. El broche a los campeonatos lo pusieron en el doble sculls mixto sub-19 Blanca López y Alfredo Mena, también vigentes campeones europeos, que se colgaron el bronce tras superar a los brasileños Helena Beatria Ewald y Joao Pedro Franca en una regata que sentenciaron al inicio del tramo de vuelta a la playa. Con anterioridad se habían impuesto a los británicos Elyssa Stoker y Jacob Lloyd en octavos y en cuartos a los polacos Rozalia Figurska y Antoni Borysewicz, pero en las semifinales no pudieron con los portentosos chinos Liu Lili y Su Juntao, que antes del ecuador ya llevaban una ventaja notable, por lo que los españoles decidieron bajar el ritmo y reservar fuerzas para luchar por el bronce. En otras pruebas de categoría sub-19, la australiana Maddison McLaughlin, luego subcampeona, acabó con las esperanzas de Marina López en cuartos, misma ronda en la que perdieron en el doble sculls Sara Torres y Lirios Huélamo ante las griegas Despoina Ermeidou y Eleni Laskaridi.

articles.title: La jueza del caso Nassar, diez años después: "El dinero y las medallas siguen por encima de la seguridad"
articles.standfirst: Rosemarie Aquilina, que en 2018 condenó al exmédico del equipo de Estados Unidos, afirma que apenas se han producido cambios que contribuyan a que los deportistas estén seguros
articles.summary: Rosemarie Aquilina, que en 2018 condenó al exmédico del equipo de Estados Unidos, afirma que apenas se han producido cambios que contribuyan a que los deportistas estén seguros
articles.body: Diez años después de que salieran a la luz los abusos cometidos por Larry Nassar, médico del equipo de gimnasia de Estados Unidos, la jueza que le condenó en 2018, Rosemarie Aquilina, afirmó que los derechos humanos deben tener prioridad sobre el deseo de éxito deportivo. Durante una reunión en Rotterdam de activistas, supervivientes y defensores de Gymnasts for Change International (G4CI), manifestaciones en las que cuestionan por qué apenas ha habido cambios en la política deportiva y qué se puede hacer al respecto, la jueza hizo hincapié en que “el caso de Nassar fue hace 10 años y ha habido muy pocos cambios significativos”. Aquilina explicó que “no busco pequeños cambios por los que mucha gente se lleva el mérito, quiero un cambio significativo y todavía no hemos llegado a ese punto, ni en el deporte, ni en la vida, ni en los tribunales, ni en las aulas, ni en el poder legislativo". La magistrada asegura que "si pregunto por qué, la respuesta es la misma: se trata de dinero, medallas y notoriedad, por encima de la seguridad de los niños, y la seguridad es un derecho humano”. Por su parte, Claire Heafford, superviviente de abusos en el deporte y directora ejecutiva de Gymnasts for Change International, declaró que "seguimos en una situación en la que no se escucha a las víctimas y en la que la magnitud de la reforma no está a la altura de la magnitud de las revelaciones". La ex gimnasta acrobática de élite Eloise Jotischky, que se convirtió en la primera persona en ganar un caso civil contra la Federación Británica de Gimnasia por los abusos que sufrió entre 2016 y 2018, que incluyeron técnicas inapropiadas de control de peso y abuso verbal, dijo que ha habido algunos cambios, pero el problema radica en su implementación. “Aún queda mucho por hacer. Por ejemplo, la Federación Británica de Gimnasia ha publicado varias políticas, como las de hidratación y las de control de peso. Eso es fantástico, pero hay que implementarlas. Si no, ¿de qué sirven?”.

articles.title: España-Euskadi: padre contra hijo en el Mundial de Pelota
articles.standfirst: Joxi Lopetegi, con España, jugó dos puntos contra su hijo Xuban, que representa al equipo del País Vasco en la modalidad de xare
articles.summary: Joxi Lopetegi, con España, jugó dos puntos contra su hijo Xuban, que representa al equipo del País Vasco en la modalidad de xare
articles.body: El enfrentamiento entre España y Euskadi en el Mundial de Pelota que se celebra en Buenos Aires (Argentina) escenificó un duelo entre padre e hijo en la modalidad de xare, durante uno de los partidos del pasado domingo La dupla española, formada por Santi Hualde y Sebastián Moncada, ganaba a la pareja vasca de Xuban Lopetegi y Markel Mujika por 15-3 y 13-6 en el segundo set. En ese instante, el seleccionador español sacó del partido a Hualde y metió en pista a Joxi Lopetegi, padre de Xuban. Ambos se enfrentaron en los dos últimos tantos del partido. El segundo set y, por extensión el partido, se cerró con un 15-6 para los españoles. Ayer, Xuban Lopetegi, junto a Oier Iturbe, cayeron ante los franceses Driolet y Lafargue, vigentes campeones del mundo, por 5-15 y 5-15. Si ganan ante Uruguay podrán disputar el partido por el bronce. Joxi Lopetegi fue campeón del mundo en 1998 y subcampeón en 2022 con España. Fue el mismo quien pidió a sus compañeros y al seleccionador jugar en algún momento contra su hijo si el encuentro así lo permitía, según cuenta a El Diario Vasco. Joxi hubiera jugado con el País Vasco pero no había logrado la clasificación para esta especialidad. En aquel momento la Federación Vasca todavía no había sido admitida como miembro de pleno derecha de la Federación Internacional. Las renuncias posteriores de Estados Unidos y Portugal abrieron la puerta al equipo de xare de Euskadi gracias a una invitación. Joxi ya estaba inscrito con España. Pidió a la Federación Española que le liberara pero no se lo concedió: "Lo entiendo porque al final les estaba pidiendo que prescindieran de una persona que les daba ciertas garantías y además para reforzar a un rival", comenta Joxi Lopetegi en el Diario Vasco.

articles.title: Asian Para Games: 1-2 for India! Pranav Soorma, Ram Ratan Singh clinch discus gold and silver
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India continued to swell their medal tally at the Asian Para Games 2026 as Pranav Soorma and Ram Ratan Singh secured a memorable one-two finish
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India continued to swell their medal tally at the Asian Para Games 2026 as Pranav Soorma and Ram Ratan Singh secured a memorable one-two finish in the men's discus throw combined F51/52/53 event on Tuesday, with Soorma setting a new Asian record to clinch gold.The 32-year-old Soorma produced a best throw of 11.66m in his fourth attempt to take the top spot, while compatriot Singh, 31, claimed silver with an effort of 10.35m in his second attempt. Both athletes compete in the F51 classification.The result added another gold and silver to India's growing medal haul at the continental para-sport event in Aichi-Nagoya, with the Indian duo delivering a standout performance in the field.Soorma adds another gold to his Asian Para Games collectionSoorma continued his impressive run at the Asian Para Games after winning gold in the men's club throw F51 event at the previous edition in China. His record-breaking effort in the discus throw further underlined his credentials as one of India's leading para-athletes.Singh complemented his compatriot's performance with a silver-winning throw, ensuring India occupied the top two positions in the event.Iran's Alireza Hemami, competing in the F53 classification, finished with the bronze medal after recording a throw of 20.20m in the fourth round.Raza points system decides final standingsAlthough Hemami registered a longer distance than both Indian athletes, he finished third because the combined event's standings were determined using the Raza Point System.The system adjusts performances according to athletes' disability classifications, converting results into standardised points to allow fair comparisons between competitors with different levels of impairment.The F51 classification includes athletes with significant limitations in trunk, leg and hand movement, alongside varying restrictions in arm function. Events may combine athletes from different classifications when participation numbers are limited.The F51-F57 categories cover seated throwing events for athletes with various lower-body impairments, limb deficiencies and limitations in muscle power or range of movement.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
