articles.title: MITB Penta, Never-Ending Feud on Life Support, a Familiar Pattern Emerges, More WWE Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The October 19 edition of Raw on Netflix featured more Bloodline vs. 946 drama and some massive action featuring title contenders, all in the Pechanga Arena San Diego in San Diego, California.
articles.body:
The October 19 edition of WWE Raw on Netflix featured more Bloodline vs. 946 drama and some massive action featuring title contenders at the Pechanga Arena San Diego in San Diego.

Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn faced off for the first time since both captured world championships, and The OTC followed up by taking the fight to The 946 with The Usos and Solo Sikoa.

Penta took down Bron Breakker with the help of Je'Von Evans. Chad Gable again defended his Intercontinental Championship successfully. Lola Vice defeated Lyra Valkyria thanks to a timely Bayley intervention.

This was the foundation of an important show as WWE heads toward Crown Jewel on November 7. Check out all the fallout from Raw below.

WWE Should Be in No Rush to Have Penta Cash In His MITB Contract

Penta is Mr. Money in the Bank, and he looks extremely confident carrying around the briefcase.

In some ways, he is already carrying himself as a world champion, which makes the luchador a big deal every time he appears.

With this in mind, WWE should not rush the cash-in. Penta could continue to taunt the world champions while he chooses the perfect time to strike.

The luchador could wait until the next major WWE show in Mexico or at least call his shot at a major premium live event, whether it be the Royal Rumble or WrestleMania.

A quick cash-in disrupts the stories of both world champions and would take longer-term story builds off the table.

Especially if Penta is going to have a lengthy run as champion, WWE should establish a clear direction for his reign before giving him the title rather than hot-shotting the change for immediate buzz.

Lola Vice, Not Iyo Sky, Should Be Next Women's Intercontinental Champion

Iyo Sky has pinned women's intercontinental champion Raquel Rodriguez, and with that win, she is likely the next in line to challenge for the gold.

While The Genius of the Sky would be a great titleholder, she does not need the belt right now, especially with multiple younger, less proven stars waiting for their shot.

In particular, WWE has set up Lola Vice as an immediately credible threat coming off an NXT Women's Championship reign. She even holds her own pinfall over Rodriguez.

While Rodriguez is a veteran who deserved a singles accolade, it is time to move on to a younger star such as the 28-year-old Vice.

WWE needs to keep building fresh names, and Sky losing to Rodriguez only for Vice to pull off the win would solidify the former MMA fighter as a real threat on Raw.

Lyra Valkyria, Bayley Need a Classic to Save Never-Ending Feud

Is there a bigger story on Raw that WWE has fallen short on building than the rivalry between Lyra Valkyria and Bayley?

Since Valkyria's initial heel turn, WWE has been noticeably inconsistent in its presentation of her.

Despite Valkyria's two wins over Bayley, The Role Model still feels more important to the weekly product. The Valkyrie's frequent absences from television have not helped.

Next week, the two will collide in a No Disqualification match that may end this story.

The match needs more than strong action; it needs a memorable moment that gives this rivalry lasting significance.

This could mean Bayley and Valkyria pulling off the best spot of the night in the ring or a brawl outside of the ring that leads to a memorable fall in the backstage area.

The goal should be to convince fans that these two matter, and whatever comes of this rivalry, both should be moving into the title picture afterward.

Not Every Week Needs to Focus on Bloodline vs. 946

Professional wrestling is built on the back of a variety of stars that work hard to get serious chances to shine. It is a variety show every week.

Despite this, Raw does not feel like it has much variety. Every week recently has closed on 946 battling The Bloodline, no matter what is booked for the night.

This show could have ended with "All Ego" Ethan Page making a statement at the expense of Chad Gable, selling his chances of becoming the next Intercontinental champion.

Instead, the show ended once again with the same groups fighting, building toward the inevitable WarGames battle that should not be the immediate focus of the current product.

The OTC should be focused on Sami Zayn while more brawling between these crews could have happened backstage.

Survivor Series: WarGames Build Eclipsing Crown Jewel Hype

Crown Jewel is the next big show for WWE, but Raw has not been building nearly as much to that PLE as Survivor Series: WarGames.

The biggest angle on Raw is The Bloodline vs. 946. The first act of that rivalry will culminate in a battle inside WarGames.

It is good to know WWE has built hype for this angle enough to create a genuinely engaging team vs. team battle for Survivor Series.

However, it is not the time to go full steam ahead on WarGames. Roman Reigns should not be brushing off and insulting Sami Zayn as a lesser champion.

Chelsea Green and Liv Morgan should be fighting and arguing in more substantial segments than random tag team matches.

If there is no real desire to make Crown Jewel's matches matter, why even deliver the show, especially when Survivor Series clearly does matter to Raw?

articles.title: 5 NHL Teams That Could Already Be Regretting Their 2026 Offseason Pickups
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NHL season isn't even a month old yet, but several teams are already struggling through the early going.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NHL season isn't even a month old yet, but several teams are already struggling through the early going.

Some of those clubs made significant moves this summer via trades and free agency, hoping to better their rosters. So far, several of those acquisitions haven't worked out as hoped.

It's still early in the season, and things could improve as those pickups adjust to the new teammates and surroundings. However, it's also possible those additions won't work out as planned.

Here's a look at five teams that could already be regretting their offseason acquisition

Notable offseason additions: Defensemen Bowen Byram and Ian Cole, forwards Patrick Kane, Jordan Greenway, and Cole Smith.

Chicago's rebuild has spun its wheels despite having young superstar Connor Bedard and promising youngsters like Anton Frondell and Frank Nazar in the lineup. Management tried to speed up the process with several veteran additions, but the club stumbled out of the gate with a 3-6-0 record by Oct. 19 .

Byram was the most notable pickup, acquired with Greenway from the Buffalo Sabres on June 23 . He subsequently signed a six-year contract extension with an average annual salary of $12.5 million. The 25-year-old wanted to prove himself as a No. 1 defenseman, but the results have been underwhelming thus far.

Bedard's early absence due to a shoulder injury and the birth of Byram's twin daughters on Oct. 3 contributed to his slow start. With Bedard back in the lineup, Byram's production from the blue line should improve. For now, however, he has one point in six games as he tries to find his footing with his new club.

Kane spent the best years of his future Hall of Fame career in Chicago, and received a hero's welcome from their fans. However, the 37-year-old winger's best seasons are in the past and he can no longer carry this team as he did in his prime.

Greenway and Cole are depth additions providing a physical defensive element to Chicago's roster. Both were among the few players on the roster with positive plus/minus numbers .

Still, the focus remains on Byram and Kane. If they can't help this club make strides toward playoff contention this season, management could start to feel the heat.

Notable o ffseason a dditions: Forwards Matthew Knies, Valeri Nichushkin, Ryan Lomberg, defensemen Emil Andrae and Carson Soucy, and goaltender Cam Talbot.

After missing the playoffs for the sixth straight season , the Columbus Blue Jackets made several notable roster additions. The biggest was acquiring Knies from the Toronto Maple Leafs in a multi-player deal that sent winger Kirill Marchenko to Toronto before the start of the regular season.

Knies had an immediate positive impact with two goals and three points in his first game with the Blue Jackets. However, he was held to one assist in his next six games , while Marchenko has nine points in as many games with the Maple Leafs.

The oft-injured Nichushkin is a skillful two-way winger when healthy. However, he hasn't played up to his usual standard, managing three points in his first six games with the Blue Jackets. The 31-year-old's physical style over his 12-season career could be catching up to him.

Lomberg, Andrae, Soucy, and Talbot are depth additions. Apart from Lomberg's feisty energy , the rest haven't done much to stand out consistently for the Blue Jackets, who are off to another erratic start.

Head coach Rick Bowness ripped his players for a poor showing in an embarrassing 7-3 loss to the Florida Panthers. More lopsided losses could be in the works if the new additions fail to perform as expected.

Notable offseason additions: Forwards Erik Haula, Mats Zuccarello, Corey Perry, and defenseman Erik Gustafsson

The retirement of long-time captain Anze Kopitar left the Kings with a big gap at center. The versatile Haula was brought in to provide short-term depth and experience at that position or on the wing if necessary.

Zuccarello and Perry were also free-agent veteran additions to provide extra depth to their forward lines. Zuccarello, 39, was coming off back-to-back 54-point seasons with the Minnesota Wild. The 41-year-old Perry had 17 goals and 37 points in 72 games split between the Kings and Tampa Bay Lightning last season.

Gustafsson, 34, was signed to bring more mobility and experience to the left side of their blueline. He also previously played under head coach Peter Laviolette. Like Haula, Zuccarello, and Perry, he came at an affordable price .

However, these additions failed to make the Kings a younger, faster team. As of Oct. 19 , they were the only team without a win.

Zuccarello appeared in three games before going on injured reserve . Gustafsson was a healthy scratch for two games, and Perry had yet to dent the scoresheet. Only the 35-year-old Haula had a decent start, with three points in his first six games.

The Kings could become sellers in the trade market if they don't reverse their fortunes soon. Some of those summer additions could find themselves skating with new clubs before the March 1 trade deadline.

Notable offseason additions: Goaltender Joseph Woll, defenseman Simon Benoit, forwards Noel Acciari, and Jack Studnicka.

The Philadelphia Flyers made the offseason's most impactful signing, inking Anaheim Ducks center Leo Carlsson on July 3 to a five-year offer sheet worth an average annual value of $18 million.

That deal briefly made the 21-year-old Carlsson the NHL's highest-paid player, directly contributing to the sharp increase in player salaries. It would've also given the Flyers the true first-line center they desperately needed, but the Ducks retained Carlsson by matching the offer .

Had the gambit to sign away Carlsson succeeded, the Flyers might have had a better start than their woeful 1-6-3 record in their first 10 games . He would've given them the much-needed offense that they're currently lacking, as they were outscored 34-14 during that stretch.

Getting Woll from the Toronto Maple Leafs this summer has worked out well thus far, with a 2.77 goals-against average and a .916 save percentage as of Oct. 19 . As for the others, they don't bear sole responsibility for the Flyers' poor performance, but they haven't really helped either.

The Flyers saved their cap space to sign Carlsson. When it fell through, there was no Plan B to put that money toward other notable options. The best talent remaining in the trade and free-agent markets were either gone by then or the asking prices were far too high.

Notable offseason additions: Forwards Nick Robertson and Hendrix Lapierre, and defensemen Kaeden Korczak, Trevor van Riemsdyk, and Declan Carlile.

After exceeding expectations by reaching the playoffs last season, the Pittsburgh Penguins continue to transition toward a younger roster. Part of the process has been bringing in established NHL players in their mid-twenties , like Robertson, Lapierre, Korczak, and Carlile.

Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas knew Robertson from their days with the Toronto Maple Leafs. He got off to a promising start with two goals in the Penguins' season opener, but has managed only two more goals since.

Lapierre spent his last three seasons trying to crack a deep Washington Capitals roster. He had three points in his first two games skating on the top line with Sidney Crosby, but was moved off that line when Bryan Rust returned. He went scoreless in his next four and was a healthy scratch in their last three games.

Korczak earned more playing time as a defensive blueliner and could flourish in that role. Meanwhile, van Riemsdyk has been sidelined since Oct. 10 with a lower-body injury . Carlile began with four points in his first three games, but the 26-year-old blueliner's production has since dried up, and he's struggled defensively.

Korczak could be a solid addition for the Penguins, but the struggles of Robertson and Lapierre stand out as the Penguins stumbled through a 1-5-1 slump leading up to their Oct. 19 game with Utah. Their lack of production could become an ongoing issue if the Penguins keep sliding in the standings .

Stats via NHL.com . Salary info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: Trade Ideas for the Flyers' Travis Konecny Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: Even with Monday night's surprising win over the Colorado Avalanche, it has not been a great start to the season for the Philadelphia Flyers. That slow start has already kick-started the rumor mill regarding one of their veteran players, forward Travis Konecny.
articles.body:
Even with Monday night's surprising win over the Colorado Avalanche, it has not been a great start to the season for the Philadelphia Flyers. That slow start has already kick-started the rumor mill regarding one of their veteran players, forward Travis Konecny.

Even though the Flyers were a playoff team in 2025-26, there was still an expectation that they might take a step backwards this season, and general manager Danny Briere made it clear that is a possibility they were prepared for when the season began.

Even with the playoff appearance, it is still a team that is in a rebuild and looking to build something long-term. It's not necessarily just about this season.

Konecny has been a key part of the organization for a while, and one of the Flyers' best players, but given his age and the team's apparent longer-term timeline there is a chance he could get eventually get moved.

Especially if the team does not turn things around this season.

While there is no indication that is on the verge of happening anytime soon, it is still something to keep an eye on. We already looked at some teams that could have an interest should it get to that point , so let's look at some of those teams and try to take a guess at what some trade ideas might look like. Or at least try to get a sense on what the value could be.

What would Travis Konecny's trade value even look like?

Trade values are never as simple as what a player is doing or producing right now in this moment.

You are not just trading for a player capable of scoring X number of goals this season in X number of games.

There is more to it than that. A lot more to it.

You are trading for that player's production, their all-around defensive game, their skill, their positional value, their age, their contract, their injury history, and every other variable that goes into determining a player's overall value and impact on a team.

From a production standpoint, Konecny is a steady, 25-goal, 60-point winger that always seems to be at the center of something chaotic happening on the ice. He would fit in with most contending teams in a top-six role, and in a vacuum is the type of player most general managers would love to have on their team.

The biggest issue and hurdle with a potential Konecny move is his no-movement clause that will allow him to control where he goes, and if he goes anywhere at all. So it's not only a matter of the Flyers having a willingness move him, it's having a willingness, along with getting an offer they deem to be acceptable, and it being to a team that he would be willing to play for.

You are going to have to think contending team here.

The other potential roadblock would be his contract and his age.

He is in year two of an eight-year, $70 million contract that runs through the end of the 2032-33 season. Given that Konecny is already 29 years old (and turns 30 in March of this season), that contract is going to run through his mid-30s.

While he is still a very good and very productive player right now, there is also a good chance he has already played his best, most productive hockey and would be joining a new team on the downside of his career. That has to be a consideration. It does not mean he is going to suddenly cease to be productive. It just means that what you see right now is probably the absolute best you are going to get from him, while also accepting the reality that it will eventually get worse. How much worse, and how quickly it gets worse, remains to be seen.

While the $8.5 million salary cap number is probably more than fair value right now, especially under the rising cap, NHL teams do not tend to value wingers, in their mid-30s, that still have term remaining on their contract as major trade chips. They can usually find competent scoring wingers in a lot of different ways without having to take on big money and give up big assets for a player that doesn't play a premium position and might have already played his best hockey.

Is Konecny still young enough (and productive enough) to make teams look past that? Maybe.

The Flyers don't have any pressure to move Konecny at this point and might need to be blown away to consider it, so let's take a look at what that might mean in terms of value.

Philadelphia receives: Alexander Nikishin, prospect Charlie Cerrato, first-round pick

Trading within the division might not be something Philadelphia is very keen on doing, but the Hurricanes have salary cap space, trade assets, and are very much in a win-now mode.

Nikishin is their most obvious trade chip, especially as he remains unsigned as a restricted free agent, and they would almost certainly like to move him. The most likely trade involving Nikishin is some sort of a three-team deal involving Connor Hellebuyck going to the Hurricanes, but adding another goal-scoring option to what is already one of the deepest rosters in the NHL could be a good way to set themselves up for a repeat Stanley Cup run.

Nikishin is also at an age that would fit in well with some of the Flyers' young core group of forwards, specifically Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone.

Along with Nikishin, Carolina has four first-round picks over the next three years and there is a very good chance that at least one, and maybe more, of those picks get moved for more immediate help.

Cerrato would also be an intriguing prospect to add into the Flyers organization given his role as a center and the Flyers' long-term need for more help down the middle.

Philadelphia receives: Matthew Savoie, prospect Tommy Lafreniere, 2027 first-round pick

As strong as the Oilers early season record is, they have to be self-aware enough to know that is entirely due to the dominance of Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard, and that the rest of the offense still has a lot of issues from a depth perspective.

They still need to worry about goaltending.

They probably need to address all three of those issues to some degree over the next few months. Konecny would be a big addition at forward and give them another legitimate top-six winger to help round out the lineup.

The Oilers farm system and young talent is extremely weak, but Savoie has shown flashes of being a good player and could fit into the Flyers young core and timeline. Lafreniere is an intriguing prospect, but is still probably a ways off. Given the Stanley Cup-or-bust mentality the Oilers should have right now, pretty much every first-round pick should be on the table.

NHL Teams That May Be Regretting Their 2026 Offseason Pickups

Philadelphia gets: Prospect Michael Hage, prospect Tyler Thorpe, future first-round pick, Philip Danault (cap dump)

The Flyers know they need help down the middle, and somebody that can be an impact player in a top-six role at the position. We know they know that because they tried to get Leo Carlsson on a restricted free agent offer sheet over the summer.

It didn't work, but it was a worthy effort.

Hage has top-six center potential and is one of the best prospects in a deep Canadiens system.

Montreal figures to be major buyers at some point this season following back-to-back playoff appearances and a run to the Eastern Conference Final, and while a second-line center should be high on their list, I'm not sure they would pass up the opportunity to add another top-six winger. This is an excellent team set up for long-term success, but it is not quite a finished product just yet.

Hage would give Philadelphia a really intriguing center prospect, while Thorpe is a big, physical prospect that would have the potential to fit in with the Flyers style of play and become a fan favorite if he panned out.

Danault is included just to help make the money work this season (he is in the final year of a $5.5 million per year contract).

Philadelphia receives: Tij Iginla, first-round pick , Kevin Stenlund (salary dump)

If you are not already taking Utah seriously as a potential Stanley Cup contender in the Western Conference, you need to start doing so. Their young talent is for real, and they can skate with any team in the NHL.

If they are going to make a big trade this season (and they should absolutely try to do so), Connor Hellebuyck might be the more logical target given their questions in goal. But adding a winger like Konecny could fill a potentially big stylistic need. While so much of their core is built on speed and skill, Konecny can still provide some secondary scoring and also bring a different element to their forward group with his gritty play and willingness to mix things up.

Utah has developed a strong farm system, and while Iginla is a top prospect, the Mammoth prospect pool has become deep enough they might have a willingness to part with him in the right deal. Especially given the arrival and development of players like Caleb Desnoyers, Ethan Belchetz, Thomas Lavoie and Dmitri Simashev. When you are starting to become a contender, you can't have many untouchables in your prospect pipeline.

Iginla has position flexibility at this point to play on the wing or down the middle, and is a big-time talent that could still be a long-term building block for a Flyers team that needs more gamebreakers offensively. Or at least potential gamebreakers.

articles.title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels' somber reaction to Terry McLaurin injury
articles.summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels spoke on Terry McLaurin's injury after the game: 'I love Terry.'
articles.body:
When the Washington Commanders had their best season in 33 years in 2024, quarterback Jayden Daniels and wide receiver Terry McLaurin were the primary reasons for that success. Daniels had a spectacular rookie season, and he helped lead McLaurin to his best NFL season, catching a career-high 13 touchdown passes, plus three more in the playoffs.

When the Commanders struggled in 2025 and finished 5-12, Daniels and McLaurin were on the field together only three times. Daniels and McLaurin played only one complete game together, so it wasn't surprising the offense took a significant step back.

Through the first five games this season, Daniels has missed two games and McLaurin one. In last week's tie with the New York Giants , they returned, with McLaurin playing on an ailing hamstring and still finished with four receptions for 62 yards.

On Monday night, Daniels and McLaurin were on the field against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers, and so were Stefon Diggs and Chig Okonkwo, meaning the quarterback would have his top weapons on the field together for the first time since Week 1.

On Washington's first drive, Daniels found McLaurin for a 27-yard completion, which set up a field goal to make it 7-3.

Unfortunately, that was the only time the two connected on Monday night; McLaurin suffered a non-contact injury in the first half and was carted off the field. It didn't look good. His teammates surrounded him, as did a few 49ers. Daniels was seen on the ground, checking on McLaurin.

The two are close. Daniels has always expressed his respect and appreciation for McLaurin. McLaurin has also shared his appreciation for his young quarterback.

After the game, head coach Dan Quinn said the Commanders are concerned about the significance of McLaurin's injury. That would be a brutal loss for Washington.

Afterward, Daniels shared his thoughts on McLaurin's injury.

"You see how hard he works, and you never want to wish any injury on nobody on that field because you know how much you put into the sport that you love, your body and stuff like that," Daniels said. "I didn't see the full play, but praying for Terry, man. He's been there for me through a lot since I came into this league and through the adverse times I went through last year and so far this year, he's been right there by my side. I love Terry, man. He's like a brother to me, and I appreciate him a lot."

Many Washington fans echo Daniels' sentiments on McLaurin. He's been the heart and soul of the organization since arriving in 2019. McLaurin has been through multiple name changes, multiple regime changes, and numerous quarterback changes, and through it all, he's led by example—on and off the field—and kept putting up outstanding numbers.

articles.title: Knicks guard Josh Hart shares his go-to routine before tipoff
articles.summary: New York Knicks guard Josh Hart shared the exact pregame routine he follows before every game, from eating Mike and Ikes and popcorn to drinking C4 Energy.
articles.body:
Josh Hart's pregame routine isn't built around a complicated nutrition plan. Instead, the New York Knicks guard says he sticks with a collection of familiar favorites, including Mike and Ikes, popcorn, C4 energy drinks, grapes and PB&Js, before every game.

As the Knicks prepare for a new season following their championship run, the 31-year old told USA TODAY he's not changing the ritual that's helped him feel ready to compete for years.

What Josh Hart eats before every Knicks game

"I always eat the same meal, hit the hot tub," Hart said. "Every time I eat Mike and Ikes, popcorn, grapes, PB&J, kind of a random assortment of snacks, but it works. Sitting on the bench, I pray, drink some C4, and then I'm ready to run like a bat out of hell."

While his snack choices may be unconventional, one part of Hart's routine has become an official partnership.

Earlier this year, the Knicks guard teamed up with C4 Energy , the sports drink brand he says he uses before games.

"I'm proud to join C4 and their roster of top athletes because they reflect how I show up every day: focused, disciplined, and ready to give my all," Hart said earlier this year.

"C4 fuels the effort I can control on the court, and being NSF Certified for Sport gives me full confidence in what I put in my body, making this partnership a natural and authentic fit."

Seven months after announcing the collaboration, the NBA star teased a new flavor that may come out soon. While he didn't say exactly what the flavor is, he said if he could create his own drink, it would be a Mike and Ike collab. "I feel like that would be a fun collab."

How Hart spends his offseason away from basketball

While playing professional basketball has dominated most of his life, the father of two said he tried to escape the athletic world as much as possible this past off season.

"I just kind of get as far removed from basketball as I can. I work out, but that's about it," Hart said. "This offseason, I went to Bordeaux and Capri with my wife and some friends. That was fun, definitely the highlight."

Josh Hart jokes about podcast co-host Jalen Brunson

Off the basketball court, Hart still works with Brunson, but as a co-host of their podcast, "Roommates," which stems from the two being roommates back in Villanova. Although Brunson may be a good podcast host, Hart jokes that his toddlers make better roommates.

"They're messy, they're loud but they are cute. Their cuteness outweighs everything, and JB is not that cute."

articles.title: Stefon Diggs: It's still wide open for us
articles.summary: The Commanders fell to 1-4-1 when the clock ran out on Monday night, but wide receiver Stefon Diggs chose to accentuate the positive in the locker room after...
articles.body:
The Commanders fell to 1-4-1 when the clock ran out on Monday night, but wide receiver Stefon Diggs chose to accentuate the positive in the locker room after the game.

Diggs's third quarter touchdown catch was part of a 14-point run that pared down a 20-point 49ers lead and gave the Commanders a chance to move ahead late in the fourth quarter. A long drive ended on fourth down in the red zone and the 49ers moved to 6-0 with a 23-17 lead, but Diggs said that the effort the Commanders showed and the fact that the 49ers are an outlier when it comes to their record are reasons to hold onto hope heading into their bye week.

"It's still wide open ," Diggs said, via Marshall Kramsky of WUSA. "Where we are and where the league is, it's kinda interesting. A weird spot right now. Nobody's kinda made it clear — that team we just played is a helluva football team. That's one of those guys that's gonna be in the running. . . . We played a decent game, we could've played a lot better. We were still in it, just like all these games we've been in the past couple weeks. We've been in it, we just gotta find a way to pull 'em out."

Diggs isn't wrong about things being open in the NFC East. No team in the division has won a game since Week 4 and two of the other three teams in the division have lost their starting quarterbacks for the season, so the prospect of someone running away with things feels remote. That said, the Commanders have consistently fallen short in the biggest moments of games and that provides little reason to think they're going to suddenly go on a run of their own.

The door is open for Diggs and company to prove otherwise, however, and that's about all you can ask for after winning once in six weeks.

articles.title: Patriots' Latest Receiver Addition Has A Chance To Become An Unexpected Story
articles.summary: Romeo Doubs' move to injured reserve created a sudden opening, and New England turned to a receiver with recent big-play production.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots did not wait long to react after losing Romeo Doubs. On Monday, the team placed the wide receiver on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and added Ryan Miller to its practice squad. The quiet move could become important in a suddenly complicated receiving situation.

Doubs injured his shoulder while catching a 42-yard touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 victory over the New York Jets. His placement on injured reserve means New England will be without him for at least four games, a significant development for a player who leads the team with 261 receiving yards and shares the team lead with three touchdown catches.

Ryan Miller Brings An Interesting Recent Resume

Miller is not a familiar name to many Patriots fans, but he has already appeared in regular-season NFL games. The 26-year-old receiver spent time with Miami this season, catching three passes for 92 yards and a touchdown in five games before the Dolphins released him on Oct. 13. Those numbers are limited, but they show he has produced an explosive play in a real game.

The Patriots announced Monday that Miller has appeared in 30 career games, including six starts, with 17 receptions for 254 yards and four touchdowns. New England signed him to the practice squad, so he has not automatically been added to the active roster. Still, the timing of his arrival makes his progress worth following.

Doubs is not the only injured receiver. Mack Hollins was already on injured reserve, leaving the Patriots with fewer experienced options as they prepare to visit the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. A.J. Brown returned from his own injury Sunday but caught only three of 10 targets for 27 yards. DeMario Douglas supplied seven receptions for 86 yards and a touchdown.

New England Needs Options, Not A Miracle

Miller does not have to replace Doubs' entire role to justify the signing. The Patriots still have Douglas, Brown, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III, and Hunter Henry remains a trusted target at tight end. What New England needs is enough available depth to preserve the flexibility of Josh McDaniels' passing game.

The short turnaround increases the urgency. Thursday's game at Chicago kicks off at 8:15 p.m. ET, leaving limited practice time for a new receiver to learn the offense. Whether Miller is elevated immediately or remains an emergency option, his arrival illustrates how quickly New England's plans have changed.

A week ago, the conversation centered on how many playmakers Drake Maye had around him. Now it includes whether a recent practice-squad addition might be needed to keep that group functioning.

articles.title: Penalty tracker: Texas turns in clean performance against Florida
articles.summary: With just one penalty, Texas had arguably the best performance in the Sarkisian era in avoiding flags.
articles.body:
In a disappointing loss to the Florida Gators, a bright spot for the then-No. 7 Texas Longhorns came via penalties, or rather the lack thereof. With concerns becoming increasingly worrisome as the season progressed, the Longhorns turned in arguably their best game in the Steve Sarkisian era in being flagged just one time for 15 yards.

With just one call against the Longhorns, this marks the first time in Sarkisian's 74-game tenure at Texas that his team has been flagged less than twice in a single game. In four different games during the Sarkisian era, including against Ohio State this season, Texas has committed two penalties, but never fewer.

The Longhorns now rank tied for 38th in penalties per game and 59th in penalty yards per game in the FBS, an improvement of 30 spots in the former category and 34 spots in the latter category.

The lone flag on Saturday was an illegal block below the waist on defensive back Graceson Littleton. Rather than 3rd and 1 at the Texas 40-yard line, the Florida offense was granted a fresh set of downs at the Texas 25-yard line. The drive resulted in a field goal.

Given the trajectory of the season and consecutive losses, much of the focus on the Texas football program is directed elsewhere; however, the performance on Saturday regarding penalties should be commended by the team, especially after the last few games have featured costly mistakes.

Considering the outcome, the disappointing element of the loss was how frequently the Gators made costly mistakes in committing seven penalties for 55 yards. Most notably, Florida lined up to go for it on a 4th and 1 near midfield, but a false start forced the Gators to punt instead. Head coach Jon Sumrall's team also committed a pass-interference penalty on the first Texas drive that ended in a touchdown and a face-mask penalty on the second Longhorns drive that ended with a field goal.

articles.title: Cardinals WR takes shot at Rams for losing to Mike LaFleur
articles.summary: Kendrick Bourne wants everyone to know how important Mike LaFleur was to Sean McVay and the Rams' offense.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are catching criticism after their Week 6 loss, with Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Kendrick Bourne taking a shot at his NFC West rival on social media.

Following Arizona's 18-16 win over Los Angeles on Sunday, Bourne posted on Instagram : "Them boys ain't the same wit out LaFleur."

Bourne was referring to Mike LaFleur, the Rams' former offensive coordinator who left the organization to become the Cardinals' head coach. Bourne knows the NFC West well, too, after spending multiple seasons with the San Francisco 49ers before joining Arizona this offseason. He finished the game with five receptions for 47 yards.

The Rams struggled to put away their division rival despite taking a late lead. Matthew Stafford connected with tight end Colby Parkinson for a 6-yard touchdown with 47 seconds remaining, giving Los Angeles a 16-15 advantage.

However, Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett quickly moved the Cardinals into field-goal range, and kicker Chad Ryland drilled a 43-yarder as time expired to seal the victory.

The defeat dropped Los Angeles to 2-4, while Arizona improved to 2-4 with its second consecutive road win in the Los Angeles area.

articles.title: Dan Quinn replacements: Ranking 7 best candidates if Commanders move on from coach
articles.summary: Washington may be headed to making another coaching change after only three years.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders went 12-5 in the first season under head coach Dan Quinn in 2024. Since then, ahead of Week 6 of the 2026 NFL regular season, his team has posted a 6-15-1 record, putting his job security in serious jeopardy in Year 3.

Beyond the lack of success in the past two seasons, the Commanders' botching of a potential overtime victory over the Giants in Week 5 has made his seat hotter. Quinn will need Washington to show improved results soon to extend his term to four years.

Should owner Josh Harris want to make another change and hire the 32nd head coach in franchise history, here would be his options, starting with one in-house.

Commanders' 7 best coaching candidates for 2027

1. David Blough, Commanders offensive coordinator (age: 31)

Would the Commanders follow the Bills ' example and remove an older defensive-minded coach in Quinn (56) and promote his offensive coordinator? Don't rule it out, despite Blough, a former journeyman backup, being so young.

Bold offensive-minded hires have worked well for several teams. It's a good bet Washington pivots from old-school defense to new-school offense with its new leader. Blough should get a chance because of good early work getting Jayden Daniels back on track.

2. Nate Scheelhaase, Rams offensive coordinator (age: 35)

Like Blough (Purdue), Scheelhaase is another former Big Ten quarterback (Illinois) to consider. Going back to before Sean McVay, five former Rams OCs (Mike LaFleur, Liam Coen, Matt LaFleur, Kevin O'Connell, Brian Schottenheimer) are current NFL head coaches, making the position the ultimate springboard. Scheelhaase also would get the best out of Daniels.

3. Declan Doyle, Ravens offensive coordinator (age: 30)

The Commanders also should be paying attention to what's happening with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley around the Beltway in Baltimore. Doyle left Ben Johnson and the Bears to take play-calling duties. The results have been pretty good with the Ravens as Todd Monken's replacement. Consider Quinn's original OC was Kliff Kingsbury, who did well with the Daniels because of early good experience with another running QB, Kyler Murray. Doyle would be a great fit in Washington.

4. Grant Udinski, Jaguars offensive coordinator (age: 30)

Staying offensive-minded, another hot young candidate is in Jacksonville. Grant Udinski is doing well as Coen's mentee, helping Trevor Lawrence live up to his immense physical talent. Youth might be Udinski's only barrier. Even wunderkinds Brady and Kellen Moore had to wait a little for teams to be comfortable.

5. Aden Durde, Seahawks defensive coordinator (age: 47)

Quinn got his head-coaching opportunities thanks to his acumen as a defensive coordinator, first in Seattle under Pete Carroll and later in Dallas. Durde, a British-American, has been a rising star since working under Quinn for the Falcons and Cowboys . He raised his credentials working with Mike Macdonald to lead the Seahawks championship defense. Durde deserves his shot as head coach soon.

6. Anthony Campanile, Jaguars defensive coordinator (age: 44)

The Jaguars ' coaching staff under Coen has been spot-on. Campanile also is crushing it for an active playmaking defense. Should the Commanders want to stay on Quinn's side of the ball with their head coach, this would be another strong choice.

7. Chris Shula, Rams defensive coordinator (age: 40)

Shula was in play as a potential new head coach for teams in the busy 2026 hiring cycle. He will be mentioned to get his real chance in '27 with every opening, but he doesn't make as much sense for the Commanders than the rest above.

articles.title: Seahawks add Jackson Acker, Josiah Deguara, guard Anthony Bradford to practice squad
articles.summary: The Seahawks made significant moves Monday, adding two players to their practice squad and announcing the return of a key member of their starting offensive...
articles.body:
The Seahawks made significant moves Monday, adding two players to their practice squad and announcing the return of a key member of their starting offensive line.

The team started the day Monday by adding fullback Jackson Acker and tight end Josiah Deguara.

Acker went undrafted at the 2026 NFL Draft and was later signed by the Bills. The Bills released Acker after their first preseason game, according to Seahawks.com Senior Reporter John Boyle .

Deguara is a veteran tight end, spending time with the Green Bay Packers, Jacksonville Jaguars, Arizona Cardinals, San Francisco 49ers, New York Giants, and, most recently, the Philadelphia Eagles. Throughout his seven years in the NFL, Deguara has played in 78 games, has 53 catches, and three touchdowns.

To make room for Acker and Deguara, the Seahawks released Malick Meiga and Seattle-native Dontae McMillan.

In addition to the two new additions, the Seahawks announced Monday the return of starting right guard Anthony Bradford.

Bradford, who has been on injured reserve since sitting out the second week of the season, has been dealing with both knee and hip injuries .

If everything goes to plan this week with Bradford's time at practice, Seahawks Head Coach Mike Macdonald is ready to play the experienced right guard.

"I know, normally, I'm pretty coy on this one, but it's pretty straightforward: if he has a good week, he's going to play a significant amount, if not the whole game," Macdonald said in a press conference Monday.

The Seahawks face the Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, Oct. 25, at Lumen Field. Kickoff is slated for 5:20 p.m.

articles.title: Everything Indiana’s Curt Cignetti said ahead of Michigan week, after Ohio State
articles.summary: Curt Cignetti addressed the loss to Ohio State, the final play in said loss, his team’s health and more on Monday.
articles.body:
Indiana football head coach Curt Cignetti addressed the media on Monday for his usual game week press conference following this past Saturday's 19-15 loss to Ohio State and ahead of this weekend's game at Michigan.

Here's what he had to say, courtesy of ASAPSports (edited).

CIGNETTI: Get ready for Michigan, impressive team, especially on defense. But great effort on Saturday. Great football game. We fell short, plain and simple.

Gave great effort. Had our opportunities for sure. In in some ways we beat ourselves, which is uncharacteristic of this football team, but I think we certainly proved we're capable. We just have to clean up a couple areas and use this setback to learn and grow and come back stronger and better.

So really tough opponent this week, Michigan. Made quarterback the second half at Penn State. Gave them a shot in the arm. Scored three second half touchdowns to win the game.

Really impressed with their defense. Their quickness, their tenacity, the way they played play in and play out, the way they run to the ball. It's top flight defense.

Offensively they've got good running backs. Quarterback came in and played really well. The other quarterback, you know, has a cannon and can run; makes a lot of plays with his legs.

So they'll be feeling pretty good about themselves after that victory. It will be a very physical football game again, our eighth game in a row, so looking forward, not backward, and this will be a very tough challenge.

Q : How did you assess Josh Hoover's performance after watching the film and what did you see from him?

CIGNETTI: I thought he made good plays. There are some he would like to have back, some overthrows for sure.

Q : When a quarterback is missing, overthrowing, does that tell you anything about maybe what's kind of the challenge he's facing, or what was going wrong with him?

CIGNETTI: It's just an accuracy issue. You know, there have been a couple other overthrows in games, so. Made a lot of good plays too, so.

Q : Nick and Charlie have been I think two of those most targeted receivers in the conference through whatever number of games this season. Both really talented players. What's the balance for a quarterback to wanting to really feed guys that are that talented and also maybe not wanting to get overly locked in on one or two receivers?

CIGNETTI: Well, it's not like he goes shopping what I want to pick up at the store today. The play has a certain read progression attached to it versus defenses, and quarterback goes through his progressions. We try to get those guys the ball because they're our best two playmakers.

CIGNETTI: Yeah, I mean, teams like Ohio State, Michigan, they don't give up much rushing yardage. We did have some positive runs. We got into kind of a throw mode. I they we called 46 passes and 26 runs, which is very uncharacteristic of us.

So, you know, all starts up front. We all want more consistent production, explosive plays. Haven't got any explosive plays the last two weeks in the run game.

Q : With special teams, the two missed field goals, what did you see from Nico? And in hindsight, do you wish you put Paddy McAteer out there for the long one, or did he show you something early in the season that made you think Nico was the choice there?

CIGNETTI: No, you know, that first miss was an uncharacteristic miss. We should have been in the end zone the play before but weren't. The 55 yarder would've been go for it and called the play and they came on defensively and didn't like the look. So called timeout and decided to kick it. I did think about Paddy.

We went into the game 56, Paddy 55, Nico was 55. He hit it right down the middle that would've been good from 53, because he's improved his range.

Q : (Regarding Michigan's quarterbacks and preparing.)

CIGNETTI: You can see what you need to see in the second half of Penn State in my opinion, which I watched. You know, I would assume it would be him. Could be two quarterbacks on the field at the same time. That would not surprise me. They did a lot of that at Utah.

And the other guy can make plays. So schematically they didn't change a whole lot in the second half.

Q: You guys gave Ohio State a lot of problems with your defense. Is it just a matter of coming together with the reps and playing together this long that you guys have really — what has allowed that to happen?

CIGNETTI: The defense rose to the occasion. Hey, let's face it, it was a big contest and our defense played well, played really well. The entire team played with great effort.

We met a lot of our goals. They did spit a few runs, but we gave up a little bit schematically to double cover the receiver and we know that this guy might catch a few more, they may hit a few more runs, but put pressure on the quarterback, which we wanted to do.

Then forced catches, and the one big one was an underthrow which we just kind of one of those things. But, you know, we're really good up front and the coverage was tight. Really proud of the way we played. Held them to field goals when they got down there. Created two turnovers. Set up our first score.

I thought it was an outstanding effort and we're going to need another one this week.

Q : (Regarding talking with Nick Marsh since Saturday and playing in Ann Arbor)

CURT CIGNETTI: Yeah, right. Well, we got a lot of guys hurting after this game, and that play wasn't all on Nick. There are three, four things that happened on that play that lead to a break down in execution.

So I'll see Nick tonight in the team meeting. Nick will be fine. He played well. He had one or two plays he would like to have back, but had some pressure on that play in Josh's face, and Josh's drop wasn't exactly corrected and then he punt faked it, so he could have gotten it out a little quicker.

Q : On the offensive line how have you seen them adjust to these Big Ten defensive fronts and what improvements would you like to see them make?

CIGNETTI: I thought we protected well. Be nice to get some explosive runs going again, but we did — we had a couple drives where we got some nice runs, and we're starting to, you know what I mean, and then it became a throw game.

Basically we lost the game. Like before you win it you can't lose it. You look at the second quarter. We had momentum; we're taking control. We go down there and score, we'd be up 11. We don't execute something that's like day one in terms of level of execution required.

Have to kick the field goal. Hit the crossbar. Doesn't happen very often. They go down and score. Big turn of events even first series second half. Completed pass. Strip and fumbles the ball. You know, next time went four for four. They gave us a certain look. We didn't adjust. Sack, fumble.

So those are the kind of mistakes. And then the last play of the game that we normally don't make that we make.

So, you know, I think we were all feeling pretty bad after the game that night I'm sure. I woke up, you know, with kind of a new perspective. We proved that we're capable. Just got clean up a couple things and get a little better in certain areas, so…

Q : Coach, how did you feel like you evaluated your players' ability to mentally flip from Ohio State to Michigan? Do they need on influence from the coaching staff to get in the right mindset or do you think your leaders did a good enough job?

CIGNETTI: I mean, look, this business and what we ask of players is not easy stuff; this is hard. It took a lot of effort. It was a physical game. A lot of guys, you know, felt a lot better ten days ago than they do right now, and we're heading into another one and one more after that and then we finally get an open week after nine games.

But we got to suck it up and go. Got no choice.

CURT CIGNETTI: Yeah, I would say we're optimistic on him.

Q: (On playing eight straight games including Michigan and if that changes the usual process at all)

CURT CIGNETTI: Yeah, we try to keep them healthy and fresh best we can the entire season. At this point in the year, there may be a slight tweak, but not major.

articles.title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Won vs. the Falcons
articles.summary: With the return of some superheroes, Chicago traveled to Atlanta and got the W. Here are @BryanOrenchuk’s top 3 reasons why.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears traveled to Atlanta this week to take on the Falcons and imposed their will from start to finish. Here are my top three reasons Chicago won the game. Let's get to it!

Call it competitive fire, juice, edge, 'want-to,' whatever works for you. From the opening kickoff through the closing seconds, the Chicago Bears simply wanted this game more than Atlanta. Despite what many people realize, that matters even at this level. Chicago came out to play in this one, and you could tell it meant something to them in all three phases. I'd be remiss not to mention the masses of Bears fans that traveled to Atlanta for this one too.

From the kickoff teams blowing up ball carriers, to the punt team perfectly executing some "Banana Balls" to Caleb Williams igniting the offense on the field or defense on the sidelines, these Bears were going to go down swinging. An encouraging sign after last week's defeat at Lambeau. Zavier Scott looks like an absolute keeper on this team, and his juice on special teams stands out. Daniel Hardy had himself a game both in the third phase AND on Defense with Montez Sweat out. Noah Sewell made his presence felt as well and the contrast between what Kalif Raymond brings to what his predecessor Olamide Zacchaeus brought is night and day – and that's only the reserve players! When you have your stars putting forth that same selfless effort to win games (spoiler alert – like the two guys listed below) then you have a fighters chance every week. And when your stars are as talented as they are in Chicago, good things can happen. REALLY good things. I might even call them super.

Caleb heard all the noise, yes. But in my opinion, his biggest motivating factor is and has always been winning ball games as starting quarterback and leading his team to new heights. Well, he made quite the impression Sunday, completing over 80% of his passes with zero turnovers and 1 TD pass, in addition to a career-best mark for consecutive completions with 12 straight complete throws. And that doesn't count the multiple throw aways he had either. Caleb was on fire. When he is healthy and playing like that, this offense will be hard to stop. Remember, Chicago didn't even have their RB1B in Kyle Monangai this week either. I said it on Bears Over Beers last week that I hoped he learned from Case Keenum how explosive this offense can be even without him playing Superman in the pocket and not only did he allude to it leading up to this game, but it showed on the field. Chicago has playmakers at each position. All he has to do is get it to them. On Sunday, he did just that with EIGHT players securing at least 2 catches. Caleb is back, people. Cannot wait to see him at home this week against last year's MVP runner-up and fellow 2024 rookie classman, Drake Maye. Expect fireworks.

Not to be outdone by the epic return of Caleb Williams AKA Iceman, Kyler Gordon AKA "Spider Man" or "Spidey" had arguably the most impressive performance of the afternoon. Easing back into full-time action this week, Spidey played only 16 defensive snaps. In those snaps, he accumulated 4 tackles, 3 sacks, 3 tackles for a loss, 2 forced fumbles, and 2 QB hits. Spider Man is an absolute terror for opposing offenses, and we didn't really even get to see him in coverage, where he is equally as dangerous.

After all he's been through with the public outcry over missing so much action and reports of tension in the locker room, it was huge to see his performance this week and earn himself a game ball from Ben Johnson postgame. With the struggles this defense has had to start the season, particularly in the secondary, Gordon's return couldn't have come at a better time as Chicago has the Patriots, Seahawks, and Buccaneers before the Week 10 BYE – and ALL in Primetime.

What about you? What stood out most in your mind when watching The Beloved come away with the win?

articles.title: SEC All-American Xavier Atkins no longer at Auburn, announces transfer plans
articles.summary: An SEC All-American will be able to sign elsewhere this offseason.
articles.body:
SEC All-American linebacker Xavier Atkins is no longer listed on Auburn's 2026 roster and has been dismissed from the team, according to reports .

It was announced last week, ahead of the Tigers' game against Georgia, that Atkins would miss the game due to a disciplinary issue. But head coach Alex Golesh declined to share what happened for Atkins to miss one of Auburn's biggest games of the season.

"We'll keep it in house. That'll be the only piece of it that I will be addressing. He won't be available for us this week for the game," Golesh said before the Georgia game.

The Tigers would go on to upset Georgia , 27-24, and on Monday, Golesh said they were still working through whatever happened with Atkins.

"We're still working through it. I don't have an update right now," Golesh said.

Atkins makes transfer portal plans known

While we still don't know what Atkins might've done to sit the Georgia game and then get dismissed, the star linebacker did post on his X account to announce he would be entering the transfer portal once the timing was right.

"I have nothing but respect Auburn University and will continue to support my teammates this season. My focus is on my health, my family, and on finishing up the academic semester strong, and I'll be entering the transfer portal at the appropriate time," Atkins wrote on his X post .

Atkins was second on the team this season with 37 tackles. He also had 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks, along with one interception. There is no doubt that Atkins will be a sought-after linebacker target once the transfer portal opens.

Last season, Atkins had 84 tackles, 17 tackles for loss, and nine sacks for Auburn. He was in his junior season with the Tigers and will have two more years of eligibility with the new 5-for-5 rule.
